Source: https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/google-drive.md

# Google Drive (uploads)

Your service receives files — contracts, receipts, photos — and the company
wants to see them in a Google Drive folder, not in an S3 bucket. This recipe
wires `UploadUtils` to a company folder (or Shared Drive) through a
**service account**: no user login, no consent screen.

The backend is `GoogleDriveUploadStorage`. It implements the same
`UploadStorage` protocol as the local disk and MinIO, so your upload route
does not change at all: only the object passed as `backend=`.

```bash
uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[upload,google-drive]>=0.373.0"
```

The `[google-drive]` extra brings `pyjwt` and `cryptography` (`httpx` is
already in the base package). There is no `google-api-python-client` and no
`google-auth`: a service account's token exchange is one signed JWT and one
POST, and the SDK does it itself.

## Step 1 — Get the service account and its JSON key

You leave this step with a JSON file — the service account's credential. You
can do it in the console (clicking) or with `gcloud` (copying commands); pick
one.

!!! tip "Menu names change"
    The Google Cloud console renames and reorganizes menus from time to
    time. If a name below does not match the screen, follow the official
    guides: [Create service accounts](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-accounts-create)
    and [Create and delete service account keys](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/keys-create-delete).

### 1.1 — A Google Cloud project

The service account lives inside a Google Cloud project. Sign in to the
[console](https://console.cloud.google.com/) with the company's Google account
and, in the project picker at the top of the page, choose an existing project
or click **New project**. Write down the **project ID** (e.g.
`my-company-uploads`).

### 1.2 — Enable the Google Drive API

Without it, every call to the Drive API is refused. Under **APIs & Services →
Library**, search for **Google Drive API** and click **Enable**.

### 1.3 — Create the service account

Under **IAM & Admin → Service accounts**, click **Create service account**:

1. Give it a name (e.g. `uploader`). The console suggests the **ID** and
   shows the e-mail the account will have:
   `uploader@my-company-uploads.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
2. At the roles step, **grant none** and finish. The account needs no IAM
   role on the project to use Drive: access to files comes from **sharing**
   the folder (Step 2), not from IAM.

### 1.4 — Generate the JSON key

Open the account, go to the **Keys → Add key → Create new key** tab, choose
**JSON** and confirm. The browser downloads a file like this (values
shortened):

```json
{
  "type": "service_account",
  "project_id": "my-company-uploads",
  "private_key_id": "3f2a…",
  "private_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n…\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n",
  "client_email": "uploader@my-company-uploads.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "token_uri": "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token"
}
```

The two things the recipe uses are the `client_email` (you need it in Step 2)
and the whole file (it goes into the settings in Step 3).

!!! warning "Key creation blocked by the organization"
    If creating the key fails with an organization-policy message, your
    Google Cloud organization blocks service-account keys (the
    `iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation` constraint). Whoever administers
    the organization can grant an exception for this project; there is no
    way around it on the SDK side, which authenticates precisely with the
    key.

=== "With gcloud"

    The whole step, for those with the [gcloud CLI](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install)
    installed and signed in (`gcloud auth login`):

    ```bash
    gcloud projects create my-company-uploads
    gcloud config set project my-company-uploads
    gcloud services enable drive.googleapis.com
    gcloud iam service-accounts create uploader --display-name="Service uploads"
    gcloud iam service-accounts keys create drive-sa.json \
        --iam-account=uploader@my-company-uploads.iam.gserviceaccount.com
    ```

    The last command writes the key to `drive-sa.json` in the current
    directory.

!!! warning "That file is a password"
    Whoever holds the JSON acts as the service account. Keep it in your
    deployment's secret manager, never in the repository — if it sits in the
    project folder during development, add its name to `.gitignore`. If it
    leaks, delete the key in the account's **Keys** tab and generate a new
    one. The SDK never writes the key, the signed JWT or the access token to
    a log or an error message, and the credentials' `repr` hides the private
    key.

## Step 2 — Share the folder with the `client_email`

The service account is an account like any other in Drive: it only sees what
is shared with it. Take the `client_email` from the JSON and choose where the
files will live.

### Shared Drive (recommended)

Shared Drives exist on **Google Workspace** accounts; a personal Gmail account
has none. In [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/):

1. Under **Shared drives**, create one (or open an existing one).
2. Click the drive name → **Manage members**, paste the `client_email` and
   give it the **Content manager** role (or higher — the backend's `delete`
   removes files, and roles below that cannot).
3. Optional: create a folder inside the drive for the uploads.

### Regular folder (My Drive)

Right-click the folder → **Share**, paste the `client_email` and give it the
**Editor** role. Read the "Why a Shared Drive" note below before choosing
this path.

### The IDs that go into the settings

Open the folder in the browser. The **folder id** is the last segment of the
URL: `https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/`**`1AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOp`** — that is
`GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID`.

If the folder is in a Shared Drive, open the drive's **root**: the last
segment of its URL is the drive id (`GOOGLE_DRIVE_DRIVE_ID`, optional — it
restricts searches to that drive). If you write straight into the Shared
Drive's root, the same value is also the folder id.

!!! info "Why a Shared Drive"
    A file the service account uploads into a person's **My Drive** folder
    is owned by the service account, and Google's documentation and forums
    describe service accounts as having no storage quota of their own — the
    upload is refused with `storageQuotaExceeded`. In a Shared Drive the
    file belongs to the company drive. This was **not measured** in this
    repository (there is no real credential here); read
    [Shared drives overview](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/about-shareddrives)
    before deciding. Every SDK call to the Drive API sends
    `supportsAllDrives=true`, so both shapes work on the client side.

### Check before wiring the service

A one-minute script proves the key and the sharing are right: it writes a
test file into the folder and deletes it.

```python title="check_drive.py"
import asyncio
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.storage.google_drive import (
    GoogleDriveUploadStorage,
)
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils import UploadResult

PROBE_KEY: str = "tempest-credentials-check.txt"


async def probe_bytes() -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
    """Yield the tiny payload of the check file."""
    yield b"tempest credentials check"


async def main() -> None:
    """Upload and delete a probe file to prove the key and the sharing."""
    storage: GoogleDriveUploadStorage = GoogleDriveUploadStorage.from_service_account(
        folder_id="1AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOp",
        credentials_path="drive-sa.json",
    )
    try:
        result: UploadResult = await storage.write_stream(
            PROBE_KEY, probe_bytes(), content_type="text/plain"
        )
        print("upload ok:", result.url)
        print("deleted:", await storage.delete(PROBE_KEY))
    finally:
        await storage.aclose()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

On success it prints the file link and `deleted: True`. On failure the
exception says what is missing:

| Exception | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GoogleDriveException` with `reason` `invalid_private_key` | the JSON's `private_key` is not a valid PEM RSA key (file edited, truncated or pasted with the wrong line breaks) | download the key again (Step 1.4) |
| `GoogleDriveFolderNotFoundException` | Drive answered `404` for the folder: wrong id, or the folder is not shared with the `client_email` (the message names the e-mail) | check the id in the URL and the sharing (Step 2) |
| `GoogleDriveException` with another `reason` | Drive refused the call for another reason (API not enabled, role without permission, quota) — `details` carries the `status` and `reason` Google sent | read the `reason` and go back to the matching step |

The exceptions and the mapping are the SDK's and are covered by the test
suite; **which** status Google returns in each case (for instance `404` for
an unshared folder) is what the [error-handling guide](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/handle-errors)
describes, and was not measured against Google in this repository.

## Step 3 — Configure the settings

Compose the `GoogleDriveSettings` mixin:

| Variable | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS_PATH` | path to the service-account JSON |
| `GOOGLE_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS_JSON` | the whole JSON, inline (wins over the path when both are set) |
| `GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID` | the folder files are written into |
| `GOOGLE_DRIVE_DRIVE_ID` | optional: the Shared Drive holding the folder — searches are restricted to it |

```bash
GOOGLE_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS_PATH=/run/secrets/drive-sa.json
GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID=1AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOp
```

`settings.google_drive_kwargs()` returns a `GoogleDriveStorageKwargs`
(`TypedDict`) ready to splat into
`GoogleDriveUploadStorage.from_service_account(...)` — the type-checker
checks the splat against the signature.

## Step 4 — Plug it into `UploadUtils`

A complete service:

```python
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import UploadUtils
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.storage.google_drive import (
    GoogleDriveUploadStorage,
)
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings import GoogleDriveSettings


class Settings(GoogleDriveSettings):
    """Service settings: only Google Drive, in this example."""


settings: Settings = Settings()
storage: GoogleDriveUploadStorage = GoogleDriveUploadStorage.from_service_account(
    **settings.google_drive_kwargs()
)
uploads: UploadUtils = UploadUtils(
    backend=storage,
    max_size_bytes=20 * 1024 * 1024,
    allowed_extensions={"pdf", "png", "jpg"},
)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    """Close the HTTP client the backend created."""
    yield
    await storage.aclose()


app: FastAPI = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


@app.post("/api/contracts")
async def upload_contract(file: UploadFile) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Validate the contract and send it to the Drive folder."""
    key = await uploads.save(file, subdir="contracts")
    return {"key": str(key)}


@app.delete("/api/contracts/{name}")
async def delete_contract(name: str) -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Delete the contract from Drive (it skips the trash)."""
    return {"deleted": await uploads.delete(f"contracts/{name}")}
```

Piece by piece:

- **`from_service_account(...)`** reads the JSON, creates its own
  `httpx.AsyncClient` and builds the `GoogleDriveClient` with the
  `ServiceAccountTokenProvider`. Since it created the client, the backend
  closes it in `aclose()` — hence the `lifespan`. Pass `http_client=` to
  reuse a client of yours (then you close it).
- **`UploadUtils(backend=storage, ...)`** still validates extension, MIME,
  size and magic bytes before any byte leaves the service.
- **`uploads.save(...)`** returns the *key* (`contracts/<uuid>.pdf`). That is
  what you store in the database, as with the local disk and MinIO.

## How a key becomes a file

Drive identifies files by **id**, not by path, and accepts two files with the
same name in one folder. So the backend:

- writes the key into `appProperties` (properties private to the app), under
  `tempest_key`;
- uses the key's last segment as `name`, only for people browsing the
  folder;
- finds the file with the search
  `'<folder>' in parents and appProperties has { key='tempest_key' and value='<key>' } and trashed = false`,
  with quotes and backslashes in the key **escaped** for Drive's search
  syntax.

`exists(key)` answers whether the search finds anything; `delete(key)`
permanently deletes (`files.delete`, no trash) every match and returns
`False` when nothing matched.

!!! note "Key length"
    The [properties documentation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/properties)
    caps each property at 124 bytes (name + value, UTF-8). With
    `tempest_key` that leaves 113 bytes for the key; more is refused with
    `ValidationException` (`422`, `code="VALIDATION_ERROR"`) **before** any
    request — the message says how many bytes the property takes and names
    the 124 limit, and `details` carries `property`, `bytes` and
    `limit_bytes`. The same applies to each `metadata=` pair. The key `UploadUtils`
    generates (uuid + extension) fits easily; mind
    `keep_original_name=True` with long names.

### Same key twice: the content is replaced

Writing a key that already exists **replaces the content of that same
file**: same id, same link, new media (resumable `files.update`). No new file
is created, and `exists` keeps finding exactly one — the same behaviour as
overwriting on the local disk or MinIO.

!!! warning "Two simultaneous writes of a new key"
    As far as the Drive documentation shows, there is no conditional create
    (not measured). If two requests write the **same new
    key** at the same time, both may create a file. Then `exists` answers
    `True`, the next write replaces the first one, and `delete` removes them
    all. The default `UploadUtils` key (a uuid) does not collide.

## `presigned_url` raises

Drive **has no presigned URLs**: it serves a file to whoever holds a Drive
permission, not through a temporary signed link. So
`storage.presigned_url(key)` raises `PresignedUrlUnsupportedException`
(`501`, `code="PRESIGNED_URL_UNSUPPORTED"`) instead of returning a permanent
link someone would treat as temporary.

To serve the file to your users, write an authenticated route of your own.
When the Drive link is what you want (in an internal panel, say), use
`await storage.web_view_link(key)`; every write's `UploadResult.url` carries
that `webViewLink` too. It is **permanent** and only opens for someone with
access to the file in Drive.

### Download in the admin panel

The admin panel (`make_admin_router`) with `upload_fields` uses the same
backend. The download route of an upload field asks for `presigned_url` and,
when the backend has no presigned URL — it returned `None` **or** raised
`PresignedUrlUnsupportedException` —, looks for a permanent link: if the
backend implements the `SupportsWebViewLink` protocol
(`async def web_view_link(self, key: str, /) -> str | None`), the route
answers `303` to that link. `GoogleDriveUploadStorage` implements it, so the
admin download **redirects to the Drive link**, which only opens for someone
with access to the file there. With no link (file deleted in Drive, or a
backend of yours without `web_view_link`) the route falls back to the usual
path: a local file, or `404` "file not available".

A backend of yours that wants the same only needs the method:

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils import SupportsWebViewLink


class MyStorage:
    """Example: a backend with a permanent link per key."""

    async def web_view_link(self, key: str) -> str | None:
        """Return the file's permanent link, or None."""
        return f"https://files.example.com/{key}"


assert isinstance(MyStorage(), SupportsWebViewLink)
```

## Resumable upload, in pieces

The backend uses Drive v3's
[resumable upload](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/manage-uploads#resumable):

- The stream goes up in pieces that are multiples of 256 KiB (`chunk_size=`,
  8 MiB by default) — memory holds a little over one piece (a piece plus the
  chunk the backend reads ahead), not the file.
- Every piece but the last carries `Content-Range: bytes a-b/*`; Drive
  answers `308` with a `Range` header saying how much it kept, and the next
  piece starts right after. Bytes Drive did not keep are re-sent; nothing
  else is.
- The backend reads **one piece ahead**: a piece only goes out with `/*` once
  more bytes are known to follow it. So the last `PUT` always carries bytes
  **and** the total (`bytes a-b/<total>`), including when the size is an
  exact multiple of the piece (256 KiB, 512 KiB, 8 MiB…). An empty
  `bytes */<total>` `PUT` is also how a session is **queried**; ending the
  upload with one left a fake HTTP server that treats it as a query stuck in
  `upload_stalled`. The exception is the **0-byte** file, which has no byte to
  carry: it closes with `bytes */0`.
- Retried with exponential backoff (0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s…, up to 16 s), up to
  `max_retries` times (5 by default): `429`, `5xx`, transport errors and
  **rate-limit `403`** — Drive reports an exhausted quota as `403` with
  `reason` `rateLimitExceeded` or `userRateLimitExceeded`
  ([handling errors](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/handle-errors)).
  Any other `403` (`insufficientFilePermissions`, `storageQuotaExceeded`…)
  is raised at once. This holds for metadata calls and for pieces; on a
  piece, the backend asks the session how much it holds before retrying.
  The whole file is never re-sent.
- **`Retry-After`:** on a `429` or `503` carrying that header in seconds, the
  wait is what Drive asked for, capped at `backoff_max_seconds` (16 s by
  default); a missing header or the HTTP-date form falls back to the
  exponential backoff.
- A `308` with no progress (Drive kept none of the piece) waits the backoff
  before re-sending; after `max_retries` such answers in a row it becomes
  `GoogleDriveException` with `reason="upload_stalled"`. A `308` saying Drive
  holds **less** than it had already acknowledged — bytes the backend
  already dropped from memory — cannot be repaired and is raised at once
  with `reason="upload_range_regressed"`.
- A `404` on a piece or on the status query means the **resumable session**
  expired or was lost: it becomes `GoogleDriveException` with
  `reason="upload_session_not_found"` and a message saying to upload again —
  not `GoogleDriveFolderNotFoundException`, which is kept for the `404` of
  the search and of opening the session.
- The first read of the stream happens **before** the session is opened.
  So the `content_validator` of `UploadUtils.save(...)` (and the `validator`
  of a caller using `storage.write_stream(...)` directly), which runs on the
  first chunk, refuses without opening any session. `max_size_bytes` stops
  the stream midway, and the session is abandoned before its last piece.
  Per the
  [resumable upload guide](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/manage-uploads#resumable),
  the file is created when the session completes, so an interrupted write
  **should** leave no file in the folder — this was not measured against the
  real Google.
- When the write fails, for any reason, the backend closes (`aclose`) the
  generator you passed, so its `finally` runs right away.

## Errors

| Situation | Exception | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Folder missing or not shared (`404`) | `GoogleDriveFolderNotFoundException` — the message names the folder and the `client_email` to share it with | `502` |
| Resumable session expired or lost (`404` on a piece) | `GoogleDriveException`, `reason="upload_session_not_found"` | `502` |
| Retries exhausted (`429`, `5xx`, rate-limit `403`) | `GoogleDriveException` with the last answer's `status` and `reason` | `502` |
| Session stopped taking bytes / lost acknowledged bytes | `GoogleDriveException`, `reason="upload_stalled"` / `"upload_range_regressed"` | `502` |
| The JSON's `private_key` is not a PEM RSA key | `GoogleDriveException`, `reason="invalid_private_key"`, before any request; the message names the `client_email`, never the key | `502` |
| Any other refusal from Drive or the token endpoint | `GoogleDriveException`, with `details={"status": <http>, "reason": <error.errors[0].reason>}` (or the OAuth `error`, such as `invalid_grant`) | `502` |
| `presigned_url` | `PresignedUrlUnsupportedException` | `501` |
| Validator rejected | `InvalidFileTypeException` | `415` |
| Key (or a `metadata` property) over 124 bytes | `ValidationException` | `422` |
| Stream exceeded `max_size_bytes` | `FileTooLargeException` | `413` |

Per the [error-handling guide](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/handle-errors), Drive should answer `404` both for a
folder that does not exist and for one the account cannot see (not measured
here), so the message talks about the common case: sharing.

## Swapping the service account for another token

The token exchange sits behind the `AccessTokenProvider` protocol, a single
method (`async def access_token(self) -> str`). A user OAuth token provider
replaces `ServiceAccountTokenProvider` without touching the client:

```python
import httpx

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.storage.google_drive import (
    GoogleDriveClient,
    GoogleDriveUploadStorage,
)


class StaticTokenProvider:
    """Example: a token obtained outside the SDK."""

    def __init__(self, token: str) -> None:
        """Store the token."""
        self.token: str = token

    async def access_token(self) -> str:
        """Return the stored token."""
        return self.token


http: httpx.AsyncClient = httpx.AsyncClient()
client: GoogleDriveClient = GoogleDriveClient(
    token_provider=StaticTokenProvider("ya29.…"),
    http_client=http,
)
storage: GoogleDriveUploadStorage = GoogleDriveUploadStorage(
    client, folder_id="1AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOp"
)
```

## What was measured and what was not

The suite checks **the wire**, with `httpx.MockTransport`: the JWT (decoded
with the public half of an RSA pair generated in the test — `alg`, `kid`,
`iss`, `scope`, `aud`, `iat`, `exp`), the token POST body, the cache and the
single exchange under concurrency, the headers and `Content-Range` of each
piece, resuming after a short `308`, closing with bytes and the total on a
size that is an exact multiple of the piece (against a fake that treats an
empty `bytes */<total>` as a query), the backoff of a no-progress `308` and
the immediate error of a `308` that goes backwards, the `503`/`429` and
rate-limit `403` retry, `Retry-After` and its cap, the session `404`, the
escaped search, `supportsAllDrives` on every call, the error mapping and the
admin download redirect to `web_view_link`.

**Not measured against the real Google** (there is no credential in this
repository): service-account quota on My Drive, behaviour inside a Shared
Drive, the 124-byte property limit, the one-week lifetime of a resumable
session, the moment the file starts to exist, whether Drive closes a 0-byte
upload on the empty `bytes */0` `PUT`, the real shape of the rate-limit
`403` and of the expired-session `404`, and whether Drive sends
`Retry-After` — all of that comes from the official documentation linked
above. The test
`tests/integrations/storage/google_drive/test_live.py` does the full round
trip (upload, overwrite, check `exists`, delete) when
`TEST_GOOGLE_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS` and `TEST_GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID` are set:

```bash
TEST_GOOGLE_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS=/path/sa.json \
TEST_GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID=1AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOp \
uv run pytest -m network tests/integrations/storage/google_drive/test_live.py
```

## Recap

- `uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[upload,google-drive]>=0.373.0"`, a service account
  with a JSON key, the Drive API enabled, a folder (ideally in a Shared
  Drive) shared with the `client_email`.
- `GoogleDriveSettings` + `GoogleDriveUploadStorage.from_service_account(**settings.google_drive_kwargs())`.
- `UploadUtils(backend=storage)` — the upload route does not change.
- The key lives in `appProperties`; a repeated key replaces the content of
  the same file; `delete` skips the trash.
- `presigned_url` raises `PresignedUrlUnsupportedException`; the Drive link
  is in `web_view_link` and `UploadResult.url`, and the admin download
  redirects to it.
- The last piece always carries bytes and the total; `429`, `5xx` and
  rate-limit `403` are retried, honouring `Retry-After`; a `404` mid-upload
  is a lost session, not a missing folder.
- A Drive refusal becomes `GoogleDriveException` with status and `reason`; a
  folder not shared becomes `GoogleDriveFolderNotFoundException` naming who
  to share it with.

Source: https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/hostbridge.md

# Host control (files, commands, power)

Your service runs inside WSL and needs to act on the **machine** hosting it:
read a file under `C:\Users\...`, run a PowerShell command, open the native
file picker, power the computer down at the end of the day.
`tempest_fastapi_sdk.hostbridge` is that layer — the one that used to live
as a separate service in every project that needed it.

Nothing here mounts itself: `create_app` does not know this module, and the
router exists because a service asked for it.

```bash
uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk"
```

The system, file and command surface needs no extra at all — it is the
standard library and FastAPI. Reading PDFs needs `[pdf-read]`, and reading
them **with layout and tables** needs `[pdf-layout]`.

!!! danger "This is a shell on that machine"
    Whoever reaches these methods runs commands as the host user and powers
    the machine off. Two things follow, and neither is optional:
    `allowed_base_paths` starts **empty** — denying every path until someone
    configures it — and `make_hostbridge_router` **requires** auth
    dependencies, refusing an empty list. The write side (commands, writes,
    deletes, power) is behind `destructive=True` and off by default.

## The first read

`HostBridge` takes a `HostBridgeConfig` and nothing else. Everything is
`async`, and whatever touches the disk or a process runs off the event loop:

```python
import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.hostbridge import HostBridge, HostBridgeConfig


async def main() -> None:
    bridge = HostBridge(
        HostBridgeConfig(allowed_base_paths=("/mnt/c/Users/me/Documents",)),
    )

    info = await bridge.host_info()
    print(info.computer_name, info.os_version)

    file = await bridge.read_text("C:\\Users\\me\\Documents\\notes.txt")
    print(file.size_bytes, file.content[:80])


asyncio.run(main())
```

Look at that path: it was written in **Windows** form and it worked. The
bridge takes both — `C:\Users\me` and `/mnt/c/Users/me` — and normalizes
before checking, through `wslpath` where it exists.

!!! warning "Order matters: resolve first, check second"
    The path is resolved (`..` collapsed, symlinks followed) **before** it is
    compared against `allowed_base_paths`. Checking before resolving is the
    classic bug: `/mnt/c/Users/me/../../../etc/passwd` starts inside an
    allowed base and ends outside it.

## Configuration from the environment

In a service, these options belong on `Settings`. Compose the mixin and
splat the mapper — the field → argument translation lives in one place:

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings import HostBridgeSettings, ServerSettings
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.hostbridge import HostBridge, HostBridgeConfig


class Settings(HostBridgeSettings, ServerSettings):
    """Only what is specific to this service is declared here."""


settings = Settings()
bridge = HostBridge(HostBridgeConfig(**settings.hostbridge_kwargs()))
```

The environment variables are the field names themselves:
`HOST_ALLOWED_BASE_PATHS`, `HOST_POWERSHELL_BINARY`, `HOST_CMD_BINARY`,
`HOST_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` and `HOST_MAX_FILE_READ_BYTES`.

!!! info "`HOST_ALLOWED_BASE_PATHS` has no permissive default"
    Empty denies everything. That is the safe direction to fail: a bridge
    that can run PowerShell should not also be able to read the whole disk
    because nobody remembered to configure it.

## Exposing it over HTTP

`make_hostbridge_router` returns an `APIRouter` ready for `include_router`.
It **requires** the dependency list — the signature is what forces the auth
decision, instead of a warning in the docs:

```python
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import make_token_dependency, register_exception_handlers
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.hostbridge import (
    HostBridge,
    HostBridgeConfig,
    make_hostbridge_router,
)

app = FastAPI()
register_exception_handlers(app)

bridge = HostBridge(
    HostBridgeConfig(allowed_base_paths=("/mnt/c/Users/me/Documents",)),
)

app.include_router(
    make_hostbridge_router(
        bridge,
        dependencies=[Depends(make_token_dependency("a-long-secret"))],
    )
)
```

That mounts the side that **reads**:

| Method | Route | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/system/info` | Machine name, user, OS, uptime |
| `GET` | `/system/files` | Read a text file |
| `GET` | `/system/files/list` | List a directory |
| `GET` | `/system/files/pdf` | Extract a PDF, page by page |
| `POST` | `/system/files/pick` | Open the native file picker |

The side that **writes** — `POST /system/exec`, `POST`/`DELETE
/system/files`, `POST /system/{shutdown,restart,abort,lock,logoff}` — only
appears with `destructive=True`:

```python
from fastapi import Depends

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import make_token_dependency
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.hostbridge import (
    HostBridge,
    HostBridgeConfig,
    make_hostbridge_router,
)

bridge = HostBridge(
    HostBridgeConfig(allowed_base_paths=("/mnt/c/Users/me/Documents",)),
)

router = make_hostbridge_router(
    bridge,
    dependencies=[Depends(make_token_dependency("a-long-secret"))],
    destructive=True,
)
```

!!! tip "Turn the destructive side on only with someone there to confirm"
    An assistant that runs commands without human confirmation is one that
    deletes the wrong folder exactly once. The pattern that works is holding
    the call until the user approves it, showing the exact arguments.

## Errors, with a code

Every failure raises one of the SDK's envelope exceptions, so a service that
already calls `register_exception_handlers` answers `{detail, code, details}`
with no extra wiring — in PT-BR or en-US, per `Accept-Language`:

| Code | Status | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HOST_INVALID_PATH` | 400 | Path outside the bases, or untranslatable |
| `HOST_FILE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No file there |
| `HOST_FILE_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Over `max_file_read_bytes` |
| `HOST_FILE_DECODE_FAILED` | 400 | Bytes do not decode — a PDF or an image |
| `HOST_COMMAND_FAILED` | 500 | The command exited non-zero |
| `HOST_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` | 504 | The command ran past its timeout and was killed |
| `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | The executable the action calls (PowerShell, `wslpath`, `shutdown.exe`) does not exist here — one missing is enough |

`HOST_UNAVAILABLE` is what tells "this machine has no Windows host" apart
from "the action failed": on a plain Linux container the caller degrades
instead of reporting an error.

## Reading a PDF from the host

```python
import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.hostbridge import HostBridge, HostBridgeConfig
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.pdf import PdfExtractorEnum


async def main() -> None:
    bridge = HostBridge(
        HostBridgeConfig(allowed_base_paths=("/mnt/c/Users/me/Documents",)),
    )
    document = await bridge.read_pdf(
        "C:\\Users\\me\\Documents\\contract.pdf",
        extractor=PdfExtractorEnum.LAYOUT,
    )
    for page in document.pages:
        print(page.page_number, len(page.tables), page.text[:60])


asyncio.run(main())
```

`PdfExtractorEnum.TEXT` is `pypdf` — fast, plain prose, `[pdf-read]`.
`PdfExtractorEnum.LAYOUT` is `pdfplumber`, `[pdf-layout]`: slower, but it
recovers columns and fills `page.tables`.

!!! warning "There is no OCR here"
    A scanned page is an image with no text layer: it comes back with
    `text=""` rather than being dropped — entry `n` is always page `n`.
    Check for it and route those files elsewhere; handing a model an empty
    page is how a confident answer gets invented about something nobody read.

## Running commands

```python
import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.hostbridge import (
    CommandSchema,
    HostBridge,
    HostBridgeConfig,
)


async def main() -> None:
    bridge = HostBridge(HostBridgeConfig())
    result = await bridge.run_command(
        CommandSchema(command="Get-Date -Format o", shell="powershell", timeout=10),
    )
    print(result.return_code, result.stdout.strip(), result.duration_seconds)


asyncio.run(main())
```

!!! note "Elevation (UAC) does not happen from here"
    A command that needs administrator rights fails. Wrap it through `gsudo`
    or a pre-created Task Scheduler entry on the Windows side.

## Recap

- `HostBridge` + `HostBridgeConfig` give you the whole surface;
  `HostBridgeSettings` is the same thing from the environment, via
  `hostbridge_kwargs()`.
- An empty `allowed_base_paths` denies everything, and a path is resolved
  before it is checked.
- `make_hostbridge_router` requires auth by signature, and only mounts the
  write side with `destructive=True`.
- Every failure carries a `code` — `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` says this machine has
  no host to control.
- PDFs: `[pdf-read]` for text, `[pdf-layout]` for columns and tables, no OCR
  in either.


---

Source: https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/genai-hosted.md

# Hosted generative AI (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google)

The SDK's AI base runs local models — `TextGenerator` (transformers) or
`OllamaGenerator` (daemon). Sometimes the number that matters is not RAM but
**cost per token**, or you need a model that does not fit on your machine.
That is what the hosted backends are for:

| Provider | Backend | Generation + stream | Tool calling | Structured output | Embeddings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | `AnthropicGenerator` | yes | yes | yes (`json_schema`) | — |
| OpenAI | `OpenAICompatGenerator` | yes | yes | yes (`json_schema`) | `OpenAICompatEmbedder` |
| DeepSeek | `OpenAICompatGenerator` | yes | yes | yes (`json_object`) | — |
| Google (Gemini) | `OpenAICompatGenerator` | yes, through the compatible endpoint (untested) | yes, likewise | yes (`json_schema`) | — |

The idea is a single one: they implement **the same protocols** as Ollama —
`TextBackend` (`generate` / `chat` / `stream`), `StructuredTextBackend`
(`chat_structured`), the agent's `ToolCallingBackend` (`chat_with_tools`) and
RAG's `SupportsEmbed`. You change the line that builds the backend and the
rest of the service stays as it is.

!!! info "Installation"

    ```bash
    uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[genai-hosted]"
    ```

    The extra only pulls `httpx`, which is already a base dependency — it
    exists so the service declares the capability it uses. No vendor SDK
    (`anthropic`, `openai`) is installed.

## First step: the keys in settings

Compose the `HostedGenAISettings` mixin into the service settings:

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, HostedGenAISettings


class Settings(HostedGenAISettings, BaseAppSettings):
    """Service settings."""


settings: Settings = Settings()
```

```bash
# .env
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
OPENAI_MODEL=<OpenAI model id>
OPENAI_STT_MODEL=<transcription model id>
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-...
GOOGLE_API_KEY=AIza...
GOOGLE_MODEL=<Gemini model id>
```

Each provider has `*_API_KEY`, `*_BASE_URL` and `*_MODEL`. The defaults:

| Variable | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `https://api.anthropic.com` |
| `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` |
| `OPENAI_MODEL` | empty — required |
| `OPENAI_STT_MODEL` | empty — required by `openai_speech_kwargs()` |
| `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` | `https://api.deepseek.com` |
| `DEEPSEEK_MODEL` | `deepseek-flash` |
| `GOOGLE_BASE_URL` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` |
| `GOOGLE_MODEL` | empty — required by `gemini_kwargs()` |

!!! note "Where the defaults come from"

    `claude-opus-5-5` is the model Anthropic's models table recommends as the
    starting point (<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview>).
    `deepseek-flash` is one of the two values DeepSeek's reference accepts
    in the `model` field
    (<https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion>). For OpenAI
    the SDK pins no id: `openai_kwargs()` raises `ValueError` while
    `OPENAI_MODEL` is empty.

## Generating text

The `*_kwargs()` methods return exactly what the constructor takes, so
building the backend is a splat:

```python
import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, HostedGenAISettings
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import AnthropicGenerator, OpenAICompatGenerator


class Settings(HostedGenAISettings, BaseAppSettings):
    """Service settings."""


settings: Settings = Settings(ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-...", DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="sk-...")

claude: AnthropicGenerator = AnthropicGenerator(**settings.anthropic_kwargs())
deepseek: OpenAICompatGenerator = OpenAICompatGenerator(**settings.deepseek_kwargs())


async def main() -> None:
    """Ask both providers the same thing."""
    print(await claude.generate("Explain PIX in one sentence."))
    print(await deepseek.generate("Explain PIX in one sentence."))
    async for piece in claude.stream("Count to five."):
        print(piece, end="", flush=True)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Piece by piece:

- `AnthropicGenerator` speaks the Messages API: `POST {base_url}/v1/messages`
  with the `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version` headers
  (<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/overview>). `system` turns become
  the top-level `system` field, which is where that API reads them.
- `OpenAICompatGenerator` speaks `/chat/completions`. `deepseek_kwargs()`
  points it at `https://api.deepseek.com`; the format is the same, according
  to <https://api-docs.deepseek.com/>.
- `stream()` reads each provider's SSE events and yields only the text.

An empty key raises `ValueError` **at construction**, not a 401 from inside
the first background job.

!!! warning "`max_tokens` on Anthropic"

    The Messages API requires `max_tokens` on every call
    (<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages>).
    `AnthropicGenerator` sends `16000` when the call sets no
    `max_new_tokens`; change it with `max_tokens=` on the constructor or with
    `GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=...)`.

## The same code, any backend

This is where the swap becomes free. Write the consumer against the
protocol, not against the provider:

```python
import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import (
    AnthropicGenerator,
    OllamaGenerator,
    OpenAICompatGenerator,
    TextBackend,
)


async def summarize(backend: TextBackend, text: str) -> str:
    """Summarize a text with any backend."""
    return await backend.chat(
        [
            {"role": "system", "content": "Summarize in one sentence."},
            {"role": "user", "content": text},
        ],
    )


async def main() -> None:
    """Run the same summary on three backends."""
    backends: list[TextBackend] = [
        OllamaGenerator("llama3.2"),
        AnthropicGenerator(api_key="sk-ant-..."),
        OpenAICompatGenerator(
            "deepseek-flash",
            api_key="sk-...",
            base_url="https://api.deepseek.com",
        ),
    ]
    for backend in backends:
        print(await summarize(backend, "PIX is Brazil's instant payment system."))


asyncio.run(main())
```

`make_genai_router`, `AIChatPipeline` and `Agent` take the backend the same
way — pass the hosted one wherever you would pass `OllamaGenerator`.

## Agent with tools

`Agent` calls `chat_with_tools(messages, tools)` and reads `tool_calls` in the
OpenAI/Ollama shape. `AnthropicGenerator` translates both ways: tools go out
as `{name, description, input_schema}`, `tool_use` blocks come back as
`tool_calls` (keeping the `id`), and `role: tool` results go back to the API
as `tool_result` blocks in a single `user` turn, as the tool-use guide asks
(<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview>).

```python
import asyncio
from typing import Any

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.agents import Agent, AgentContext, AgentTool
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import AnthropicGenerator


async def add(arguments: dict[str, Any], context: AgentContext) -> str:
    """Add two integers."""
    return str(int(arguments["a"]) + int(arguments["b"]))


add_tool: AgentTool = AgentTool(
    name="add",
    description="Add two integers.",
    parameters={
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"a": {"type": "integer"}, "b": {"type": "integer"}},
        "required": ["a", "b"],
    },
    handler=add,
)


async def main() -> None:
    """Run an agent on Claude."""
    agent: Agent = Agent(AnthropicGenerator(api_key="sk-ant-..."), tools=[add_tool])
    run = await agent.run("What is 2 + 3?")
    print(run.stop_reason, run.output)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Swapping `AnthropicGenerator(...)` for `OpenAICompatGenerator(...)` or
`OllamaGenerator(...)` changes nothing else in the example.

## Structured output

`chat_structured(messages, schema)` returns a validated instance of your
Pydantic model:

```python
import asyncio

from pydantic import BaseModel

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import AnthropicGenerator, StructuredTextBackend


class Invoice(BaseModel):
    """Fields to extract."""

    number: str
    total_cents: int


async def read(backend: StructuredTextBackend, document: str) -> Invoice:
    """Extract the invoice from a document."""
    return await backend.chat_structured(
        [
            {"role": "system", "content": "Extract the invoice fields."},
            {"role": "user", "content": document},
        ],
        Invoice,
    )


async def main() -> None:
    """Extract with Claude."""
    print(await read(AnthropicGenerator(api_key="sk-ant-..."), "Invoice A-1, $5.00"))


asyncio.run(main())
```

Each provider asks for JSON differently, and the backend handles it:

- **Anthropic** — `output_config.format` with `type: json_schema`. The API
  requires `additionalProperties: false` on every object and rejects numeric
  and string-length constraints
  (<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs>);
  the schema sent is adapted, and the reply is validated against **your**
  model, original constraints included.
- **OpenAI** — `response_format` with `type: json_schema`.
- **DeepSeek** — `response_format` with `type: json_object`, the only JSON
  mode documented (<https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/json_mode>); the
  schema goes in a `system` turn at the end of the conversation, which also
  meets the requirement of the word "json" in the prompt.

## Full outcome, images and the provider from the model id

`chat_structured` answers one question — "give me the instance" — and raises
on any other outcome. Whoever pays for each call needs three more answers,
**even when there is no instance**: what the call cost, why the model stopped
and what it wrote. A refusal, a reply cut at `max_tokens` or JSON that fails
the schema were billed too.

`complete_structured` returns all of it in a `StructuredCompletion`, and
`hosted_generator` picks the provider from the model id:

```python
import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, HostedGenAISettings
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import (
    StructuredCompletion,
    StructuredCompletionBackend,
    hosted_generator,
    image_part,
)


class Settings(HostedGenAISettings, BaseAppSettings):
    """Service settings."""

    AI_MODEL: str = "claude-haiku-5-5"


class Transcript(BaseModel):
    """The text read from the photo."""

    readable: bool
    text: str


async def transcribe(
    backend: StructuredCompletionBackend,
    photo: bytes,
) -> StructuredCompletion[Transcript]:
    """Read the text of a notebook photo."""
    return await backend.complete_structured(
        [
            {"role": "system", "content": "Transcribe the text in the photo."},
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    image_part(photo, "image/jpeg"),
                    {"type": "text", "text": "Transcribe it."},
                ],
            },
        ],
        Transcript,
        effort="low",
        cache_system=True,
        max_tokens=2048,
    )


async def main() -> None:
    """Transcribe with the configured model."""
    settings = Settings()
    backend = hosted_generator(**settings.hosted_kwargs(settings.AI_MODEL))
    result = await transcribe(backend, Path("notebook.jpg").read_bytes())
    if result.output is not None:
        print(result.output.text)
    else:
        print("no result:", result.stop_reason, result.error)
    print("tokens:", result.usage)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Piece by piece:

- **`hosted_generator(model, api_key=...)`** reads the provider off the id
  prefix (`claude-` → Anthropic, `gpt-`/`o1`/`o3`/`o4`/`chatgpt-` → OpenAI,
  `gemini-` → Google, `deepseek-` → DeepSeek; the table is `MODEL_PREFIXES`)
  and builds the backend with what each provider documents: the field the
  output budget goes to (`max_completion_tokens` on OpenAI), the JSON mode
  (`json_object` on DeepSeek) and the effort values. An id outside the table
  (a fine-tune, your own server) raises `ValueError`: pass `provider=` and,
  if needed, `base_url=`.
- **`settings.hosted_kwargs(model)`** returns exactly the arguments of
  `hosted_generator` — the model, and the key and URL **of the resolved
  provider**. Changing provider becomes changing `AI_MODEL` in `.env` (and
  having that provider's key there).
- **`image_part(data, media_type)`** builds the image part in the OpenAI
  shape, which is the SDK's message shape. `AnthropicGenerator` translates it
  to a Messages API `image` block; `OpenAICompatGenerator` forwards it as is.
- **`effort`** goes out as `output_config.effort` on Anthropic and as
  `reasoning_effort` on the OpenAI format. Gemini documents `minimal`, `low`,
  `medium` and `high` (<https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai>), so
  `xhigh` and `max` become `high` (`GOOGLE_EFFORT_VALUES`). DeepSeek does not
  document the field, and neither `hosted_generator` nor `deepseek_kwargs()`
  sends it (`effort_field=None`).
- **`cache_system=True`** marks the `system` turn with
  `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` on Anthropic. The OpenAI format has
  no per-message marker, and the argument is accepted and ignored.

The `StructuredCompletion` you get back:

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `output` | the validated instance, or `None` |
| `text` | the reply as received |
| `usage` | the provider's `TokenUsage`, **whatever the outcome**; `None` when the response carries no `usage` |
| `stop_reason` | `end`, `max_tokens`, `refusal`, `tool_use` or `other` |
| `provider_stop_reason` | the original value (`end_turn`, `length`...) |
| `error` | why `output` is `None` after a natural stop |

!!! tip "Only a natural stop is parsed"

    A reply cut at `max_tokens` can validate by accident when the schema's
    last fields have defaults. So parsing only happens with
    `stop_reason == "end"`; otherwise `output` is `None` and `error` stays
    empty — `stop_reason` already says why.

!!! note "Cache written and cache read"

    `TokenUsage.cache_write_tokens` is the slice of the input written to the
    cache (Anthropic's `cache_creation_input_tokens`), which Anthropic bills
    above the base rate; `cache_hit_tokens` is the slice read. Both are
    already inside `input_tokens`. The OpenAI format reports no write, and
    the field stays `0`.

The tests for this surface run over `httpx.MockTransport`: they pin the
request each backend builds and the reading of the documented response, not
the behavior of a live provider.

## One provider chosen in `.env`

Reading the provider off the model id prefix is convenient, but it hides a
business decision inside a model name, and each provider wants its own key
variable. When the service sends **every** model to **one** provider, say so
in `.env`, with the provider, the key and (optionally) the URL:

```bash
# .env
GENAI_PROVIDER=openai
GENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
# GENAI_BASE_URL=https://internal-gateway/v1   # empty uses the provider URL
AI_MODEL_FREE=gpt-5-mini
AI_MODEL_FAMILY=gpt-5
```

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, HostedGenAISettings
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import TextBackend, hosted_generator


class Settings(HostedGenAISettings, BaseAppSettings):
    """Service settings: both models come from the same provider."""

    AI_MODEL_FREE: str = "gpt-5-mini"
    AI_MODEL_FAMILY: str = "gpt-5"


def plan_backend(settings: Settings, family: bool) -> TextBackend:
    """Build the plan's generator with the provider from `.env`."""
    model = settings.AI_MODEL_FAMILY if family else settings.AI_MODEL_FREE
    return hosted_generator(**settings.hosted_kwargs(model))


settings = Settings(GENAI_PROVIDER="openai", GENAI_API_KEY="sk-...")
print(settings.hosted_kwargs(settings.AI_MODEL_FREE)["provider"])  # openai
```

With `GENAI_PROVIDER` set, `hosted_kwargs` changes rule:

- **The provider is the one in `.env`**, for every model. An id with another
  provider's prefix (`claude-...` with `GENAI_PROVIDER=openai`) raises
  `ValueError` instead of switching provider silently; an id with no known
  prefix (a fine-tune, a model behind an OpenAI-compatible server) goes to
  the chosen provider.
- **The key is `GENAI_API_KEY`**; empty, it falls back to the provider's own
  key (`OPENAI_API_KEY`...). The URL is `GENAI_BASE_URL` or, when empty, the
  provider's.
- **A `provider=`** that disagrees with `.env` raises `ValueError`: one
  service talks to one provider.
- **Without `GENAI_PROVIDER`** (absent or empty), nothing changes: the
  provider comes from the prefix, as in the section above.

!!! check "The production boot demands the key"

    With `EnvironmentSettings` composed and `ENV=production`, a
    `GENAI_PROVIDER` with no effective key (neither `GENAI_API_KEY` nor the
    provider's own) refuses the boot, listing `GENAI_API_KEY`. A service that
    never sets `GENAI_PROVIDER` is not affected: the per-provider keys stay
    optional.

## PDFs: `document_part` and `supports_documents`

You already send images with `image_part`. PDFs have the same problem, plus
one: each provider spells the document part its own way, and not every
provider takes one. Writing the block by hand (Anthropic's `document`, for
instance) ties the service to one provider — changing `GENAI_PROVIDER` then
breaks only the PDF flow, and only in production.

`document_part` builds the part once, and each generator translates it or
refuses it:

```python
import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, HostedGenAISettings
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import (
    StructuredCompletion,
    StructuredCompletionBackend,
    document_part,
    hosted_generator,
    supports_documents,
)


class Settings(HostedGenAISettings, BaseAppSettings):
    """The service settings."""

    AI_MODEL: str = "claude-haiku-5-5"


class Agenda(BaseModel):
    """The events read from the notice."""

    events: list[str]


async def read_agenda(
    backend: StructuredCompletionBackend,
    pdf: bytes,
) -> StructuredCompletion[Agenda]:
    """Extract the events from a PDF notice."""
    return await backend.complete_structured(
        [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    document_part(pdf, filename="notice.pdf"),
                    {"type": "text", "text": "List the events."},
                ],
            },
        ],
        Agenda,
        max_tokens=2048,
    )


async def main() -> None:
    """Check the provider at boot and read the PDF."""
    settings = Settings()
    kwargs = settings.hosted_kwargs(settings.AI_MODEL)
    if not supports_documents(kwargs["provider"]):
        raise SystemExit(f"{kwargs['provider']} documents no PDF input")
    backend = hosted_generator(**kwargs)
    result = await read_agenda(backend, Path("notice.pdf").read_bytes())
    print(result.output)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Piece by piece:

- **`document_part(data, media_type="application/pdf", *, filename=None)`**
  builds OpenAI's Chat Completions `file` part: `file_data` is a base64 data
  URL and `filename` goes with it (`document.pdf` when you pass none, because
  every base64 example in OpenAI's guide sends a name). Only
  `application/pdf` is accepted; another type, or empty bytes, raises
  `ValueError` right away. Plain text goes in a `text` part.
- **Anthropic:** `AnthropicGenerator` translates the part into a `document`
  block with a base64 `source`, and `filename` becomes the block's `title`.
- **OpenAI:** `OpenAICompatGenerator` forwards the part as is.
- **Google and DeepSeek:** the generator `hosted_generator` builds for them
  (and the one `gemini_kwargs()` / `deepseek_kwargs()` build) raises
  `ValueError` **before** opening the connection when a message carries the
  part, with a message naming the provider. Text and images still go out
  normally.
- **`supports_documents(provider)`** answers the same question without
  calling anything: `True` for `anthropic` and `openai`, `False` for
  `google`, `deepseek`, `None` and an unknown name. It is what the service
  checks at boot, or before offering the PDF route. The list is
  `DOCUMENT_PROVIDERS`.

Where each row came from, read on 2026-11-04:

| Provider | What the documentation says | SDK result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | `document` block with a base64 `application/pdf` `source`, according to Anthropic's documentation (<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support>) | translates |
| OpenAI | "Chat Completions accepts only PDF files as `file` content parts", with `file_data` as a data URL, according to OpenAI's documentation (<https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/pdf-files>) | forwards |
| Google | the compatible-endpoint page (<https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai>) documents image and audio, and no `file` part | `ValueError` |
| DeepSeek | the chat reference (<https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion>) lists a `file` part, but describes `file_data` as a data URL "of the image" and names no PDF | `ValueError` |

!!! warning "The request was tested, not the answer"

    The tests for this part run on `httpx.MockTransport`: they pin the body
    each generator builds and the `ValueError` with no request sent. No
    provider was actually called — that Anthropic and OpenAI read the PDF is
    what their documentation says, not something the SDK measured. If Google
    or DeepSeek start documenting PDFs, the change is one line in
    `DOCUMENT_PROVIDERS`.

!!! tip "Generic compatible server"

    An `OpenAICompatGenerator` built by hand (vLLM, your own gateway)
    forwards the part by default (`accepts_documents=True`): the SDK does not
    know what that server accepts, and the server answers for it. Pass
    `accepts_documents=False` to refuse before the call.

## Embeddings (OpenAI)

`OpenAICompatEmbedder` implements `SupportsEmbed`, so it goes into a
`Retriever` in place of `OllamaEmbedder`:

```python
import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import OpenAICompatEmbedder


async def main() -> None:
    """Produce two vectors."""
    embedder: OpenAICompatEmbedder = OpenAICompatEmbedder(
        "text-embedding-3-small",
        api_key="sk-...",
    )
    vectors: list[list[float]] = await embedder.embed(["hello", "world"])
    print(len(vectors))


asyncio.run(main())
```

Vectors come back in input order, sorted by the response's `index`.

!!! note "Anthropic and DeepSeek have no embeddings"

    Anthropic offers no embedding endpoint, and the navigation of DeepSeek's
    reference lists Chat Completions, Responses, FIM, models, balance and
    files — no embeddings. For RAG with those providers, produce the vectors
    with `OpenAICompatEmbedder`, `OllamaEmbedder` or `Embedder`.

## Remote transcription (speech-to-text)

`SpeechToText` runs Whisper **in your process**: it downloads weights, holds
RAM (or GPU) and competes for CPU with the rest of the service. When a server
that transcribes already exists — `tempest-ai`, OpenAI itself, a `vLLM`
serving Whisper — `OpenAICompatSpeech` sends the audio to it over the OpenAI
endpoint `POST {base_url}/audio/transcriptions` and returns the same
`Transcription`.

First, the settings. The key and the root are the ones `openai_kwargs()`
uses (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`); only the model changes, in
`OPENAI_STT_MODEL`:

```bash
# .env
OPENAI_API_KEY=<tempest-ai API key>
OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://ai.buscar.app.br/api/openai/v1
OPENAI_STT_MODEL=<id that GET /models lists>
```

Then, a service that receives the upload and transcribes it:

```python
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    BaseAppSettings,
    HostedGenAISettings,
    register_exception_handlers,
)
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import OpenAICompatSpeech
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.audio import Transcription


class Settings(HostedGenAISettings, BaseAppSettings):
    """Service settings."""


settings: Settings = Settings()
speech: OpenAICompatSpeech = OpenAICompatSpeech(**settings.openai_speech_kwargs())


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    """Close the backend's HTTP client on shutdown."""
    yield
    await speech.aclose()


app: FastAPI = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
register_exception_handlers(app)


@app.post("/transcribe")
async def transcribe(file: UploadFile) -> Transcription:
    """Transcribe the uploaded Portuguese audio."""
    audio: bytes = await file.read()
    return await speech.transcribe(audio, language="pt", with_segments=False)
```

Piece by piece:

- `openai_speech_kwargs()` returns `model`, `api_key`, `base_url` and
  `provider="openai"` — the splat builds the backend. With `OPENAI_STT_MODEL`
  empty it raises `ValueError` at boot, as `openai_kwargs()` does for
  `OPENAI_MODEL`.
- `base_url` **includes** the version (`.../v1`), as with
  `OpenAICompatGenerator`; the backend appends `/audio/transcriptions`. For
  `tempest-ai`, pass `https://ai.buscar.app.br/api/openai/v1`.
- The request is multipart with `file`, `model`, `language`, `prompt` and
  `temperature` (each only when you pass it) and `response_format=verbose_json`, the format that carries
  `duration`, `language` and `segments`. The key goes in
  `Authorization: Bearer`.
- `language` takes the ISO-639-1 code (`"pt"`) or a `LanguageEnum`
  (`LanguageEnum.PT_BR` becomes `"pt"`); `None` lets the server detect it.
- `with_segments=False` returns `segments=[]`; `duration` and `language`
  are still filled.
- `prompt` hands the model vocabulary — city names, product names — and
  `temperature` pins the decode temperature. How to build the prompt and its
  token limit are in
  [Give Whisper the vocabulary](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/genai/audio.md#give-whisper-the-vocabulary-prompt-and-hotwords).
  Whether the server honours the fields is up to it: the SDK guarantees they
  go in the form.
- `audio` takes `bytes` or a local path (`str` or `Path`). A string is always
  a path, never a URL: the backend fetches nothing off the machine.

!!! tip "Drop-in for `SpeechToText`"

    `OpenAICompatSpeech.transcribe` takes the same `language`,
    `with_segments`, `prompt` and `temperature` as `SpeechToText`
    (`hotwords` is local-only) and satisfies the `SpeechTranscriber`
    protocol. Code that does
    `await transcriber.transcribe(audio, language="pt", with_segments=False)`
    does not change; and `make_genai_router(speech_to_text=speech)` serves
    `/transcribe` with it.

Server errors become exceptions that `register_exception_handlers` already
answers:

| Server status | Exception | What your client gets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401, 403 | `HostedAuthenticationError` | 500 — a wrong key is a configuration defect |
| 413 | `FileTooLargeException` (server's message) | 413 |
| 400, 422 | `ValidationException` (server's message) | 422 |
| 429 | `HostedRateLimitError` | 500 |
| 5xx | `HostedServerError` | 500 |

On `413`/`400`/`422`, `details` carries `backend`, `model`, `status` and the
`server_code` the server sent (`AUDIO_TOO_LARGE`, `INVALID_AUDIO`).

!!! warning "Speech synthesis is left out"

    `/audio/speech` uses another model (the TTS one), and
    `OpenAICompatSpeech` holds a single model. For speech, use
    `TextToSpeech` or `OllamaSpeech`.

## When the provider fails

Both backends raise the same exception family:

| Exception | Status | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HostedAuthenticationError` | 401, 403 | Fix the key — retrying will not help |
| `HostedRateLimitError` | 429 | Wait `retry_after` seconds (when the header is sent) |
| `HostedServerError` | 5xx, including Anthropic's 529 | Try later, or fall back to another backend |
| `HostedAPIError` | anything else (400, 402, 422...) | Fix the request |

All inherit from `HostedAPIError`, which inherits from
`httpx.HTTPStatusError` — code that already caught that exception from
`OpenAICompatGenerator` keeps catching it.

```python
import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import (
    AnthropicGenerator,
    HostedRateLimitError,
    HostedServerError,
    OllamaGenerator,
)


async def answer(question: str) -> str:
    """Use Claude and fall back to local Ollama when it is down."""
    claude: AnthropicGenerator = AnthropicGenerator(api_key="sk-ant-...")
    try:
        return await claude.generate(question)
    except HostedRateLimitError as error:
        print(f"rate limited; retry in {error.retry_after}s")
        raise
    except HostedServerError:
        return await OllamaGenerator("llama3.2").generate(question)


print(asyncio.run(answer("Explain PIX.")))
```

Each exception carries `provider`, `status_code`, `error_type` and `detail`
(from the provider's error body) and `request_id` (Anthropic's `request-id`
header). On Anthropic, an error can also arrive **after** the `200`, in the
middle of the stream (`event: error`,
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming>):
`stream()` raises the same typed exception — an `overloaded_error` becomes a
`HostedServerError` with `status_code` 529 — and the text already yielded
stays yielded.

!!! tip "Retry is built in"

    The SDK's HTTP client retries `429`, `500`, `502`, `503` and `504` with exponential backoff —
    on `AnthropicGenerator`, `529` too. What it does **not** retry is a read
    timeout: the provider aborts the generation when the client gives up, and
    the retry would start it again from zero.

## Why not the official SDKs

`anthropic` and `openai` are HTTP wrappers. At their current versions
(`anthropic` 1.15.0, `openai` 3.31.0), both require `httpx2` — a second HTTP
stack that the SDK's `HTTPClient` and the tests' `httpx.MockTransport` do not
reach — plus `jiter`, `anyio` and `sniffio` with upper bounds. What the SDK
uses from them is one POST and an SSE reader. Building on the `httpx` that is
already a dependency keeps retry, circuit-breaker and `X-Request-ID` the same
as Ollama's, and puts no upper bound in any consumer's lock.

## Recap

- `AnthropicGenerator` and `OpenAICompatGenerator` implement the same
  protocols as `OllamaGenerator`: change the construction, keep the rest.
- `HostedGenAISettings` + `anthropic_kwargs()` / `openai_kwargs()` /
  `deepseek_kwargs()` / `gemini_kwargs()` build the backend by splat.
- `GENAI_PROVIDER` + `GENAI_API_KEY` (+ `GENAI_BASE_URL`) pin one provider
  for every model from `.env`; another provider's model raises.
- `hosted_generator(**settings.hosted_kwargs(model))` picks the provider
  from the model id; `complete_structured` returns output, usage and stop
  reason whatever the outcome (usage, when the provider reports it), with
  images through `image_part`.
- PDFs go through `document_part`: a `document` block on Anthropic, a `file`
  part on OpenAI, `ValueError` before the call on Google and DeepSeek;
  `supports_documents(provider)` answers at boot.
- Tool calling, structured output and streaming work on all four (on Gemini,
  tool calling and streaming go through the compatible endpoint without a
  test of their own); embeddings only on OpenAI (`OpenAICompatEmbedder`).
- `OpenAICompatSpeech(**settings.openai_speech_kwargs())` transcribes on a
  remote server (`/audio/transcriptions`) and replaces `SpeechToText` without
  changing the call; `413` becomes `FileTooLargeException` and `400`/`422`
  become `ValidationException`.
- Failures become `HostedAuthenticationError`, `HostedRateLimitError` or
  `HostedServerError` — mid-stream included.


---

Source: https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/http-client.md

# HTTP client (outbound)

`HTTPClient` is a typed wrapper over `httpx.AsyncClient` for **calling
external services** with retries + exponential backoff, a circuit-breaker,
default timeouts, and `X-Request-ID` propagation. It's the outbound
counterpart of the [HTTP middleware](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/http.md) (which handles inbound
traffic). `httpx` already ships with the base package, so no extra is
needed; `[http]` still exists as an explicit (and optional) way to declare
the dependency.

## Basic usage

The client is safe to share across requests on the same event loop — it
reuses the internal connection pool. Use it as an async context manager (or
keep a singleton in [`resources.py`](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/architecture.md) and close it on the
lifespan).

```python
from typing import Any

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import HTTPClient


async def fetch_user(user_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """GET /users/{id} on the external service."""
    async with HTTPClient(base_url="https://api.example.com", timeout=10.0) as client:
        response = await client.get(f"/users/{user_id}")
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()
```

!!! warning "Don't reuse a client that's already closed"
    Leaving the `async with` block calls `__aexit__`, which closes the
    connection pool (`aclose()`). For one-off calls, build the client inside the
    `async with` as above. To reuse it across requests, keep a singleton and
    close it **once** on the lifespan (see the circuit-breaker example below) —
    never wrap each call of a shared singleton in `async with`.

Methods: `get` / `post` / `put` / `patch` / `delete` (plus a generic
`request`), all forwarding kwargs to httpx (`json=`, `params=`, `headers=`,
...) and returning an `httpx.Response`.

## Retry + backoff + circuit-breaker

Pass a `RetryPolicy` and tune the breaker thresholds at construction:

```python
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import CircuitOpenError, HTTPClient, RetryPolicy

client = HTTPClient(
    base_url="https://api.example.com",
    timeout=5.0,
    retry_policy=RetryPolicy(
        max_attempts=3,                # 1 try + 2 retries
        backoff_initial_seconds=0.5,   # 0.5s, 1s, 2s... (exponential)
        backoff_max_seconds=8.0,       # cap per wait
    ),
    failure_threshold=5,               # open the circuit after 5 straight failures
    recovery_seconds=30.0,             # half-open after 30s
    default_headers={"X-Api-Key": "..."},
    propagate_request_id=True,         # forward the current request's X-Request-ID
)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncGenerator[None, None]:
    """Close the shared connection pool on shutdown."""
    yield
    await client.aclose()


async def call() -> None:
    # Shared singleton — call it directly, no per-call `async with`
    # (that would close the pool). The pool is closed once in the lifespan above.
    try:
        await client.post("/charge", json={"amount": 100})
    except CircuitOpenError:
        # The circuit is open — don't hammer the downed upstream.
        ...
```

- **Retry**: retried on transient errors (timeouts, 5xx, connection
  failures) up to `max_attempts`, with exponential backoff capped by
  `backoff_max_seconds`. `RetryPolicy(retry_on_read_timeout=False)` takes
  `ReadTimeout` off that list and keeps the rest — see the warning below.
- **Circuit-breaker**: after `failure_threshold` consecutive failures the
  circuit **opens** and calls raise `CircuitOpenError` immediately (without
  touching the network) until `recovery_seconds` elapse, then it half-opens
  to probe.
- **Request-ID**: with `propagate_request_id=True`, the in-flight request's
  `X-Request-ID` (from `RequestIDMiddleware`) is forwarded to the upstream,
  stitching logs end-to-end.

!!! warning "`stream()` only retries before the first line"
    In `client.stream(...)`, retry and the circuit-breaker cover only
    **opening** the stream. Once the first line was yielded, a mid-stream
    failure (including a `ReadTimeout` between two chunks) propagates to the
    caller — re-sending the POST would replay lines you already consumed.
    Up to this release a mid-stream `ReadTimeout` was retried, and the
    caller saw `["Hello ", "Hello ", "world"]` from two POSTs.

!!! warning "A read timeout on an expensive call"
    A `ReadTimeout` means the request **reached** the server and the
    response did not arrive in time. On a quick call that is a stalled
    connection, and retrying fixes it. On a call whose cost is the server's
    work — a model generation — the server aborts the work when the client
    gives up, and the next attempt starts from zero with the same timeout:
    the failure arrives after `max_attempts` × the timeout instead of one.
    For those, pass `RetryPolicy(retry_on_read_timeout=False)`; a
    `ConnectError` is still retried, since no work started. The
    [`genai`](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/genai.md) generators already default to it on the client they
    build.

!!! info "Binary bodies: `stream_bytes()`"
    `client.stream_bytes(...)` has the same retry and circuit-breaker
    contract as `stream()`, but yields the body as `bytes` chunks as the
    server flushes them — audio, a file download. In both, an error status
    has its body read before the raise, so `exc.response.content` carries the
    server's message.

!!! tip "Keep it as a singleton in resources.py"
    Build the `HTTPClient` once (in `src/api/dependencies/resources.py`),
    expose a `get_http_client`, and close it on the lifespan with
    `await client.aclose()` — so the connection pool is reused across
    requests.

### The outbound header name: `request_id_header=`

`RequestIDMiddleware(header_name=...)` decides where the id is **read
from**. The name it **leaves** under belongs to `HTTPClient`: `X-Request-ID`
by default (the `REQUEST_ID_HEADER` constant), or whatever you pass in
`request_id_header=`. They are independent on purpose: each upstream expects
its own name.

```python
import httpx
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import HTTPClient, RequestIDMiddleware

seen: list[dict[str, str | None]] = []


def upstream(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
    seen.append(
        {
            "X-Request-ID": request.headers.get("X-Request-ID"),
            "X-Correlation-ID": request.headers.get("X-Correlation-ID"),
        }
    )
    return httpx.Response(200, json={})


default_client: HTTPClient = HTTPClient(base_url="http://upstream", transport=httpx.MockTransport(upstream))
partner_client: HTTPClient = HTTPClient(
    base_url="http://upstream",
    request_id_header="X-Correlation-ID",
    transport=httpx.MockTransport(upstream),
)
app: FastAPI = FastAPI()
app.add_middleware(RequestIDMiddleware, header_name="X-Correlation-ID")


@app.get("/call")
async def call() -> list[dict[str, str | None]]:
    seen.clear()
    await default_client.get("/")
    await partner_client.get("/")
    await partner_client.get("/", headers={"x-correlation-id": "manual"})
    return list(seen)


for row in TestClient(app).get("/call", headers={"X-Correlation-ID": "abc-123"}).json():
    print(row)
```

```text
{'X-Request-ID': 'abc-123', 'X-Correlation-ID': None}
{'X-Request-ID': None, 'X-Correlation-ID': 'abc-123'}
{'X-Request-ID': None, 'X-Correlation-ID': 'manual'}
```

- `default_client` forwards the id under the default name, `X-Request-ID`,
  even with the middleware reading `X-Correlation-ID`.
- `partner_client` forwards it under the name the partner expects.
- A header passed on the call wins over the propagated one, and the
  comparison ignores case: an explicit `x-correlation-id` replaces the id
  instead of sending two values.

!!! check "Since 0.341.0"
    Up to 0.340.0 the outbound name was fixed at `X-Request-ID`, and an
    explicit lowercase `x-request-id` was sent **alongside** the propagated
    id, as two values in the same header.

## The same curve outside HTTP — `async_retry`

`RetryPolicy` describes the waiting: how many tries, how long between them,
with a cap. That is not an HTTP idea — a RabbitMQ connect on boot, a push
dispatch and a third-party call all want the same curve. Only `HTTPClient`
cares about `retry_statuses`.

`async_retry` applies the curve to any coroutine:

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import RetryPolicy, async_retry

BOOT: RetryPolicy = RetryPolicy(max_attempts=5, backoff_initial_seconds=0.5)


@async_retry(BOOT, (ConnectionError, TimeoutError))
async def connect_broker(url: str) -> None:
    """Connect to the broker, tolerating a server still coming up."""
    raise ConnectionError(f"{url} unavailable")
```

Three decisions a hand-written loop tends to get wrong, made explicit here:

* **What counts as transient is yours.** The second argument is the tuple of
  exceptions that consume an attempt. Anything outside it propagates
  immediately without spending budget — a `TypeError` retried three times is
  the same bug, later.
* **The last exception propagates**, not a wrapper. A caller that knew how to
  react to a permanent `ConnectionError` still sees a `ConnectionError`.
* **Cancellation is honored.** The default `(Exception,)` lets
  `asyncio.CancelledError` through, since it derives from `BaseException` as
  of 3.8 — retrying a cancelled task fights the cancellation.

!!! warning "`max_attempts` counts the first try"
    `max_attempts=3` is one attempt plus two retries, with two waits. Zero is
    refused at decoration time: it would run the callable zero times and
    return `None` from something annotated to return `T`.


### Where the records go — `logger=`

`async_retry` writes exactly one WARNING per retry and one ERROR when the
budget runs out. The `logger=` parameter takes anything that can make those
two calls — the stdlib `logging.Logger`, or the `LogUtils` this same SDK
hands the service:

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import LogUtils, RetryPolicy, async_retry

logger: LogUtils = LogUtils(__name__)
BROKER: RetryPolicy = RetryPolicy(max_attempts=4, backoff_initial_seconds=0.2)


@async_retry(BROKER, (ConnectionError,), logger=logger)
async def publish(payload: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    """Publish to the broker, tolerating a reconnect in flight."""
    raise ConnectionError(f"broker unavailable for {payload}")
```

!!! info "The contract is `RetryLogger`, not `logging.Logger`"
    Up to 0.280.0 the annotation was `logging.Logger | None`, and `LogUtils`
    **is not** a `logging.Logger` — it wraps one. The code above ran, because
    the shapes match, and failed only under the type checker:

    ```text
    error: Argument "logger" to "async_retry" has incompatible type "LogUtils";
           expected "Logger | None"  [arg-type]
    ```

    A service without a type-checker never found out; one with a type-checker
    wrote `logger=logger.logger`, reaching under the facade. The parameter is
    now typed `RetryLogger` — a `Protocol` with `warning` and `error`, which is
    all the function uses — and both pass. Its required parameters are
    positional-only on purpose: `logging.Logger` calls the first one `msg` and
    `LogUtils` calls it `message`, and a protocol that named the parameter
    would reject one of the two under basedpyright.


## Recap

- `HTTPClient` = typed `httpx.AsyncClient` + retry/backoff/circuit-breaker + X-Request-ID (outbound name via `request_id_header=`).
- No extra required (`httpx` ships with the base package; `[http]` is optional). Methods `get/post/put/patch/delete/request` → `httpx.Response`.
- `RetryPolicy(max_attempts, backoff_initial_seconds, backoff_max_seconds)` controls retries; `retry_on_read_timeout=False` for an expensive call (generation).
- `async_retry(policy, exceptions, logger=)` applies the curve to any coroutine; `logger=` takes a `logging.Logger` or a `LogUtils`.
- `failure_threshold` / `recovery_seconds` control the breaker; `CircuitOpenError` when open.
- Share a singleton and close it with `aclose()` on shutdown.
