Source: https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/sessions.md

# Server-side sessions

Since v0.34.0 the SDK ships the full **server-side session** auth lifecycle — an alternative to the JWT flow from `UserAuthService`. The cookie carries only an opaque id; real state (user_id, TTL, client metadata, app-level data) lives in a pluggable **`SessionStore`** (Memory for dev/tests, Redis for production).

## JWT vs server-side sessions

| Aspect | JWT (`UserAuthService`) | Sessions (`SessionAuth`) |
|---|---|---|
| State | stateless (in client) | stateful (in Redis/Memory) |
| Cookie size | ~500 B – 1 KB (JWT) | 64 B (opaque id) |
| Revocation | wait for token to expire (~1h typical) | **instant** (delete the row) |
| Global logout | needs a blocklist or JWT_SECRET rotation | `revoke_all(user_id)` in one call |
| CSRF | needs custom bearer header | HttpOnly cookie; the token comes from `CSRFMiddleware` (header) or `FormCSRF` (form field, used by the [login pages](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/auth-pages.md)) — the `sessions` module ships none of its own |
| Multi-device UI ("signed in on 3 devices") | no state → impossible without extra work | `list_sessions(user_id)` is trivial |
| Multi-replica | trivial (verify-only) | requires Redis (or sticky sessions) |
| Per-request latency | none (CPU decode) | 1 Redis hit (~0.5ms LAN) |

**Use sessions when:** B2C SaaS, admin panels, SSR flows (HTMX/Django-like), instant revocation is a requirement, "active devices" UI is a feature.

**Use JWT when:** public APIs consumed by mobile/SPA, stateless microservices, high scale without a Redis dependency.

## Recipe contents

1. **[Minimum setup](#minimum-setup)** — wire 4 objects (`SessionStore`, `SessionAuth`, `SessionMiddleware`, `make_session_router`).
2. **[Bundled endpoints](#endpoints)** — login / logout / me / list / revoke.
3. **[Settings (`SessionSettings`)](#settings)** — flags + defaults.
4. **[Stores](#stores)** — `MemorySessionStore` vs `RedisSessionStore`.
5. **[How the middleware injects the session](#middleware)** — `request.state.session` + dependency.
6. **[Login without a user table](#login-without-a-user-table)** — fixed credential, HTML route with a redirect, no middleware.
7. **[Security](#security)** — anti-fixation rotation, hash-at-rest, anti-enumeration, CSRF.
8. **[Trade-offs and when NOT to use](#trade-offs)** — multi-replica, mobile, edge.

---

## Minimum setup

Four objects compose the flow. Mount once in `app.py`:

```python
# src/api/app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI

from redis.asyncio import Redis

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    AsyncDatabaseManager,
    RedisSessionStore,
    SessionAuth,
    SessionMiddleware,
    SessionSettings,
    make_session_router,
    register_exception_handlers,
)

from src.core.settings import settings
from src.db.models import UserModel

db = AsyncDatabaseManager(settings.DATABASE_URL)
session_settings = SessionSettings()

session_store = RedisSessionStore(
    Redis.from_url(settings.REDIS_URL, decode_responses=True),
    prefix=f"{settings.APP_NAME}:",
)
session_auth = SessionAuth(
    user_model=UserModel,
    store=session_store,
    settings=session_settings,
)


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(title="my-app")
    register_exception_handlers(app)

    app.add_middleware(
        SessionMiddleware,
        session_auth=session_auth,
        settings=session_settings,
    )

    app.include_router(
        make_session_router(
            session_auth,
            session_factory=db.session_dependency,
        )
    )
    return app


app = create_app()
```

!!! note "Why `Redis.from_url` here, not `AsyncRedisManager`?"
    This client feeds a **middleware** (`SessionMiddleware`), built in
    `create_app` (sync), before any async lifespan runs. `Redis.from_url()` is
    **lazy** — it constructs without opening a connection, so it fits here.
    If your service already has an `AsyncRedisManager`, prefer
    `cache.client_proxy` (v0.256.0) over opening a loose client: it is a stable
    handle, constructible before `connect()` and valid across a reconnect, and
    it keeps the manager's `disconnect()` and `health_check()`. What does not
    fit here is `cache.client`, which raises `RuntimeError` before the lifespan.
    All of them need the `[cache]` extra (the `redis` package).

Done. The user calls `POST /auth/session/login` with email+password; the SDK sets the HttpOnly+Secure cookie; every subsequent request that carries the cookie has `request.state.session` populated.

### What each object does

1. **`SessionStore`** (`RedisSessionStore` / `MemorySessionStore`) — the persistence layer. Keeps the real session state indexed by the SHA-256 hash of the opaque id. It is the only object that talks to Redis.
2. **`SessionAuth`** — the logic layer. Verifies credentials against the `UserModel`, mints, rotates, and revokes sessions through the `store`. Knows nothing about HTTP.
3. **`SessionMiddleware`** — the HTTP → session bridge. On every request it reads the cookie, resolves it through `SessionAuth`/`store`, and populates `request.state.session` **before** any router runs. Without it, `make_session_dependency()` finds no session and answers `401` even with a valid cookie — unless you pass `session_auth=` to the dependency, which then resolves the cookie itself ([no middleware](#login-without-a-user-table)).
4. **`make_session_router`** — exposes the five bundled endpoints (`login` / `logout` / `me` / `list` / `{id}`). Takes the same `session_auth` plus a `session_factory` to open the DB session on login.

!!! note "The order between `add_middleware` and `include_router` does not matter"
    Starlette builds the middleware stack on the first request, around the whole app, so `SessionMiddleware` also wraps routers included before it. Measured here (Starlette 1.6.0, FastAPI 0.141.1): with `include_router` before `add_middleware`, login answers `200` and the following `GET /auth/session/me` answers `200` too, same as the order in the example. What matters is registering the middleware **before the app starts serving**: `add_middleware` after the first request raises `RuntimeError: Cannot add middleware after an application has started`. Wire everything inside `create_app`.

---

## Endpoints

Five bundled endpoints cover the entire lifecycle:

| Method | Path | Body / Output | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/auth/session/login` | `SessionLoginSchema` → `SessionResponseSchema` | Verifies bcrypt. Mints a new session. Sets `Set-Cookie: tempest_session=<id>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`. When a previous cookie exists, **rotates** it (anti-fixation). |
| POST | `/auth/session/logout` | — → `204 No Content` | Revokes the current session and clears the cookie. Idempotent. |
| GET | `/auth/session/me` | — → `Session` | Returns the live session (`user_id`, timestamps, ip, user_agent, data). `401` when no cookie. |
| GET | `/auth/session/list` | — → `list[SessionSummarySchema]` | Lists every live session the user owns ("active devices" UI). Flags the current row with `is_current=True`. |
| DELETE | `/auth/session/{id}` | — → `204 No Content` | Revokes one specific session by its public id (first 32 chars of the hash). Clearing the cookie too when the user revokes their own session. |

---

## Settings

Mix `SessionSettings` into your `Settings`:

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, SessionSettings


class Settings(SessionSettings, BaseAppSettings):
    pass
```

```bash
# .env
SESSION_TTL_SECONDS=86400              # 24h (default)
SESSION_SLIDING=true                   # refresh expires_at on every hit (default)
SESSION_COOKIE_NAME=tempest_session
SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN=                 # None = exact host
SESSION_COOKIE_PATH=/
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true             # HTTPS only — set false only for local HTTP dev
SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=true           # JavaScript cannot read — always true
SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax            # lax / strict / none
SESSION_ROTATE_ON_LOGIN=true           # anti-fixation
```

`SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE` is `Literal["lax", "strict", "none"]` (alias `SessionCookieSameSite`). Any other value — `Strict`, `LAX`, `lax;` — fails `Settings()` construction with `literal_error`, at boot rather than on the first response. Surrounding whitespace (`lax `) is trimmed, as before.

To write and delete the cookie, use the two mappers instead of repeating seven settings in `set_cookie` and three in `delete_cookie`:

```python
from fastapi import Response

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, SessionSettings


class Settings(SessionSettings, BaseAppSettings):
    pass


settings = Settings()


def start_session(response: Response, plaintext: str) -> None:
    response.set_cookie(value=plaintext, **settings.session_cookie_kwargs())


def end_session(response: Response) -> None:
    response.delete_cookie(**settings.session_cookie_delete_kwargs())
```

`session_cookie_kwargs()` carries the cookie name as `key`, so the call site passes only the id. `session_cookie_delete_kwargs()` repeats `path`, `domain`, `secure`, `httponly` and `samesite` from the same fields — a browser only drops the cookie when the deleting `Set-Cookie` matches the `path` and `domain` it was set with. Both return a `TypedDict` (`SessionCookieKwargs` / `SessionCookieDeleteKwargs`), so mypy checks the splat against Starlette's signature. `make_session_router` uses the same mappers.

!!! danger "`SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=false` is dev-HTTP only"
    The default is `true`: the browser only sends the cookie over HTTPS. Setting `false` makes the session cookie travel in clear text over HTTP — any network intermediary can capture the id and hijack the session. Use `false` **exclusively** in local dev without TLS; never in staging or production. The same holds for keeping `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=true` (default) — turning it off exposes the cookie to XSS.

---

## Stores

### `MemorySessionStore` — dev/tests

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import MemorySessionStore

session_store = MemorySessionStore()
```

State lives in the process dict. **Does not scale** — uvicorn restart wipes everything; one replica does not see another's sessions. Use in tests and local dev.

!!! warning "`MemorySessionStore` does not survive a restart nor scale horizontally"
    State lives in an in-process dict. Every uvicorn restart/redeploy logs everyone out, and with more than one replica each worker sees only its own sessions (a cookie issued by one replica hits `401` on the other). It is strictly for tests and local dev — in production always use `RedisSessionStore`.

### `RedisSessionStore` — production

```python
from redis.asyncio import Redis

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import RedisSessionStore

from src.core.settings import settings


session_store = RedisSessionStore(
    Redis.from_url(settings.REDIS_URL, decode_responses=True),
    prefix="myapp:",
)
```

Internal schema:

- `myapp:sess:<sha256-hex>` — JSON of the `Session`, TTL = `expires_at - now`
- `myapp:user:<user-uuid>` — Redis SET of session hashes (index for `list_by_user` / `delete_by_user`)

Redis handles TTL automatically — no janitor process needed.

!!! note "`RedisSessionStore` requires the `[cache]` extra"
    `RedisSessionStore` depends on the async `redis` client, which only ships with the `[cache]` extra. Since it feeds a middleware, hand it a `Redis.from_url(...)` (lazy) or `AsyncRedisManager.client_proxy` — never `cache.client`, which raises before the lifespan. Install with `uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[cache]"` (add `auth` etc. as your service needs). `MemorySessionStore` needs no extra at all.

### Custom

Any class that implements the `SessionStore` protocol (6 async methods: `get`, `set`, `touch`, `delete`, `delete_by_user` and `list_by_user`) plugs in out of the box — DynamoDB, a Postgres table, Memcached, etc.

`touch(session) -> bool` is what makes revocation hold against a request already in flight. `SessionAuth.resolve` reads the session and writes `last_seen_at` (and the new `expires_at`, under `SESSION_SLIDING`) back through it, not through `set`. The contract: update **only if the key still exists**, in one atomic operation, without re-adding the session to the user index, and return `False` when it is gone — `resolve` then returns `None`. In `RedisSessionStore` that is a single `SET ... XX`. Without it, a `logout` or `revoke_all` that lands between the read and the write is undone: the write re-creates the session with a fresh TTL.

!!! warning "Custom store without `touch`"
    A store written before `touch` keeps working: `resolve` falls back to `set` and emits a `DeprecationWarning`, because that path cannot stop a revoked session from coming back. Implement `touch` to close the window.

---

## Middleware

`SessionMiddleware` runs **before** the routers, reads the cookie, resolves through the store, and populates `request.state.session`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import Session, make_session_dependency

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/profile")
async def profile(session: Session = Depends(make_session_dependency(required=True))):
    return {"user_id": str(session.user_id), "data": session.data}
```

**`required=True`** (default): no cookie → `UnauthorizedException` → `401` in the SDK envelope.

**`required=False`**: the handler accepts both — `session` is `Session | None`. Use on public endpoints that adapt content for logged-in users.

Direct access (no dependency):

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, Request

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import Session

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/anything")
async def handler(request: Request) -> dict:
    s: Session | None = request.state.session
    return {"authenticated": s is not None}
```

---

## Login without a user table

`SessionAuth(user_model=...)` looks the e-mail up in a table and verifies the hash. An admin panel guarded by **one** root credential from the environment has no table to point at. For that case, `SessionAuth.from_credentials(username, password, ...)` builds the service on a `StaticCredentialAuthenticator`, and `make_session_dependency(session_auth=..., on_missing=redirect_to("/login"))` guards the HTML route with no middleware at all.

The whole example — login form, protected page and logout:

```python
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Form, Request, status
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse, Response
from pydantic import SecretStr

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    BaseAppSettings,
    MemorySessionStore,
    Session,
    SessionAuth,
    SessionSettings,
    UnauthorizedException,
    make_session_dependency,
    redirect_to,
    register_exception_handlers,
)


class Settings(SessionSettings, BaseAppSettings):
    ADMIN_USERNAME: str
    ADMIN_PASSWORD: SecretStr


settings = Settings()
session_auth = SessionAuth.from_credentials(
    settings.ADMIN_USERNAME,
    settings.ADMIN_PASSWORD,
    store=MemorySessionStore(),
    settings=settings,
)
require_admin = make_session_dependency(
    session_auth=session_auth,
    on_missing=redirect_to("/login"),
)

app = FastAPI()
register_exception_handlers(app)


@app.get("/login", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def login_page() -> str:
    return (
        '<form method="post" action="/login">'
        '<input name="username"> <input name="password" type="password">'
        "<button>Entrar</button></form>"
    )


@app.post("/login")
async def login(
    request: Request,
    username: str = Form(),
    password: str = Form(),
) -> Response:
    try:
        _session, plaintext = await session_auth.login_with_credentials(
            username,
            password,
            previous_session_id=request.cookies.get(settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME),
        )
    except UnauthorizedException:
        return HTMLResponse("Credenciais inválidas", status_code=401)
    response = RedirectResponse("/admin", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)
    response.set_cookie(value=plaintext, **settings.session_cookie_kwargs())
    return response


@app.get("/admin", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def admin(session: Session = Depends(require_admin)) -> str:
    return f"<h1>Painel</h1><p>Sessão expira em {session.expires_at:%H:%M}</p>"


@app.post("/logout")
async def logout(request: Request) -> Response:
    cookie = request.cookies.get(settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)
    if cookie:
        await session_auth.revoke(cookie)
    response = RedirectResponse("/login", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)
    response.delete_cookie(**settings.session_cookie_delete_kwargs())
    return response
```

With `ADMIN_USERNAME=root`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD=s3cret` and `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=false` in the environment, driven by `httpx.AsyncClient`:

```text
GET /admin sem cookie: 303 /login
POST /login errado: 401 Credenciais inválidas
POST /login certo: 303 /admin
  Set-Cookie: tempest_session=63XC...; HttpOnly; Max-Age=86400; Path=/; SameSite=lax
GET /admin com cookie: 200 <h1>Painel</h1><p>Sessão expira em 16:55</p>
POST /logout: 303 /login
  Set-Cookie: tempest_session=""; expires=...; HttpOnly; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=lax
GET /admin com cookie revogado: 303 /login
```

(The labels are the Portuguese ones the run printed: no cookie, wrong login, right login, with cookie, logout, revoked cookie.)

### Piece by piece

1. **`SessionAuth.from_credentials(...)`** — accepts exactly one pair. Both halves are always compared, each with `hmac.compare_digest` over the value's SHA-256, and the results are combined with `&`, not `and`: a wrong username costs the same as a wrong password, and the message (`invalid username or password`) is the same for both. It takes a `SecretStr`, so the `Settings` field goes straight in. An empty credential raises `ValueError` at construction — an empty env var does not turn into "accept an empty form". It does not need the `[auth]` extra: the comparison is stdlib only, and the `PasswordUtils` (bcrypt) the `user_model=` mode uses is never built here.
2. **The session owner** is `uuid5(STATIC_CREDENTIAL_NAMESPACE, username)` by default: stable across restarts and replicas, so `session_auth.revoke_all(...)` reaches every root session. Pass `user_id=` to pick another.
3. **`login_with_credentials(...)`** — verifies and opens the session in one call. Wrong credentials raise `UnauthorizedException` without creating a session and without revoking the previous one; the route decides what to render.
4. **`make_session_dependency(session_auth=..., on_missing=redirect_to("/login"))`** — reads the cookie and resolves the session itself (with the sliding TTL, like the middleware). With no session it raises `HTTPException(303, Location=/login)`; FastAPI's handler and the SDK's `register_exception_handlers` both keep the header, and the browser follows. Without `on_missing`, the answer stays `401`.
5. **Logout** — `revoke(cookie)` deletes the session from the store (the same cookie then redirects to the login) and `delete_cookie(**settings.session_cookie_delete_kwargs())` drops the cookie in the browser.

!!! tip "Another credential backend"
    `from_credentials` is a shortcut. Any object with `async def authenticate(self, username: str, password: str, /) -> UUID` that raises `UnauthorizedException` on refusal satisfies the `SessionAuthenticator` protocol — LDAP, an upstream API — and goes into `SessionAuth(authenticator=..., store=..., settings=...)`. Pass `user_model=` **or** `authenticator=`, never both. `make_session_router` (JSON login by e-mail) needs `user_model=` and refuses, at build time, a service built with `authenticator=`.

!!! warning "`SessionMiddleware` is a `BaseHTTPMiddleware` and sits in the path of every response"
    The middleware wraps the whole app, and Starlette's `BaseHTTPMiddleware` relays every chunk of the response body through an in-memory stream. Measured here (Starlette 1.6.0, direct ASGI call with an empty `send`, median of 7 runs): a 256 MiB `StreamingResponse` in 64 KiB chunks took **~4 ms** with no middleware and **~64 ms** with `SessionMiddleware` — about 15 µs per chunk, paid by **every** route, including the upload/download that never reads the session. In a service that streams files and uses a session on three routes, prefer the dependency with `session_auth=`: only the routes that declare it pay for the lookup. If the middleware is mounted anyway, the dependency reuses the session it resolved instead of resolving again.

### `SessionAuth` built after import

In the example above the `SessionAuth` exists at import, because `Settings()` runs at module level. In a service whose settings sit behind an `@lru_cache` — which the tests clear and rebuild per test — there is no `SessionAuth` to pass when the dependency is declared. Pass a **factory** that takes the request:

```python hl_lines="25-27 34 58"
from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from pydantic import SecretStr

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    BaseAppSettings,
    MemorySessionStore,
    Session,
    SessionAuth,
    SessionSettings,
    make_session_dependency,
    redirect_to,
    register_exception_handlers,
)


class Settings(SessionSettings, BaseAppSettings):
    ADMIN_USERNAME: str
    ADMIN_PASSWORD: SecretStr


def get_session_auth(request: Request) -> SessionAuth:
    auth: SessionAuth = request.app.state.session_auth
    return auth


AdminSession = Annotated[
    Session,
    Depends(
        make_session_dependency(
            session_auth=get_session_auth,
            on_missing=redirect_to("/login"),
        )
    ),
]


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    settings = get_settings()
    app = FastAPI()
    register_exception_handlers(app)
    app.state.session_auth = SessionAuth.from_credentials(
        settings.ADMIN_USERNAME,
        settings.ADMIN_PASSWORD,
        store=MemorySessionStore(),
        settings=settings,
    )

    @app.get("/admin", response_class=HTMLResponse)
    async def admin(session: AdminSession) -> str:
        return f"<h1>Panel</h1><p>Session expires at {session.expires_at:%H:%M}</p>"

    return app
```

1. **`get_session_auth(request)`** — returns the service of the app serving the request. `make_session_dependency` calls it per request, and only when the middleware did not resolve the session first; declaring the dependency never calls it. Two apps in one process — a test that runs `get_settings.cache_clear()` and builds another — each resolve against their own: one app's cookie does not open the other's panel.
2. **`AdminSession`** — the alias lives at module level, before any `SessionAuth` exists, and routes use it as is.
3. **The type is `Session`, not `Session | None`.** With `required=True` (the default) the dependency raises instead of returning `None`, and the signature says so: no `if session is None` just for the type checker. With `required=False` the type stays `Session | None`.

---

## Security

- **Hash at rest**: the cookie carries a 32-byte URL-safe plaintext; the store keeps only the SHA-256. A leak of the `sessions` table **does not** grant logins.
- **Session-fixation prevention**: `SESSION_ROTATE_ON_LOGIN=True` (default) — a successful login always mints a fresh id, even if the browser already had one. Closes the "attacker plants a known cookie before login" vector.
- **Native CSRF via SameSite**: `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax` (default) blocks cross-site POSTs. Pair with [`CSRFMiddleware`](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/security.md) for GET-state-changing endpoints and form submissions.
- **HttpOnly + Secure**: `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True` + `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True` by default. JavaScript cannot read (anti-XSS); the browser does not send over HTTP.
- **Sliding TTL with floor**: `SESSION_SLIDING=True` (default) refreshes on every hit, but `created_at` stays put — you can force an absolute logout after N days via a job that prunes rows where `created_at < now - 30d`.
- **Anti-enumeration, in the body and in the timing**: `/auth/session/login` rejects an unknown e-mail, a wrong password and an inactive account with the **same** `UnauthorizedException` and the same message (`invalid email or password`). And all three refusals pay one bcrypt verification: an unknown e-mail is checked against a throwaway hash (`PasswordUtils.dummy_verify`), and an inactive account's password is verified before `is_active`. Measured on this machine (bcrypt cost 12, `SessionAuth.authenticate` called directly, median of N=21): wrong password **153.9 ms**, unknown e-mail **154.1 ms** — before the fix, the unknown e-mail answered in 0.4 ms. What is not bcrypt still varies (the query, the network), and the process's first refusal for an unknown e-mail pays one extra hash to build the throwaway hash. Rate-limit attempts per IP/identifier anyway: that closes brute force, which equal timing does not.
- **Instant revocation**: `revoke_all(user_id)` on password change / suspected compromise → logout on every device on the next request.

---

## Trade-offs

**When NOT to use:**

- **Public APIs for mobile** — native apps care little about cookies; bearer JWT in the `Authorization` header is still better.
- **Stateless microservices** — every replica decodes JWT without a DB hit. Sessions require a shared Redis.
- **Edge/CDN auth** — Cloudflare Workers and friends validate JWT at the edge without reaching the origin. Sessions require a backend round-trip.

**When to combine JWT + Session:**

Possible. A web SPA uses the session cookie; mobile on the same backend uses `UserAuthService.login` → JWT. Both flows coexist without conflict — `UserAuthService` and `SessionAuth` speak to the same `UserModel`, differing only in the post-verify step (mint JWT vs mint Session).

## Recap

- A server-side session is the alternative to JWT when instant revocation is a
  requirement: the cookie carries only an opaque id, and the state lives in the
  store.
- Four objects make the flow — `SessionStore`, `SessionAuth`,
  `SessionMiddleware` and `make_session_router` — mounted once in `app.py`.
- Five bundled endpoints cover the whole cycle, and the middleware populates
  `request.state.session` before any router runs.
- The cookie carries the plaintext; the store keeps only the SHA-256. Leaking
  the sessions table does **not** log anybody in.
- Without a user table, `SessionAuth.from_credentials(...)` compares both
  halves of the credential in constant time, and
  `make_session_dependency(session_auth=..., on_missing=redirect_to("/login"))`
  guards an HTML route with a `303`, no middleware. With the `SessionAuth`
  built after import, `session_auth=` takes a `(request) -> SessionAuth`
  factory, and the dependency alias comes out typed as `Session`.
- `settings.session_cookie_kwargs()` / `session_cookie_delete_kwargs()` write
  and delete the cookie with the same attributes.
- `MemorySessionStore` covers dev and tests; swap the store, not the rest of
  the wiring, to move to Redis or a database.

## Next steps

- **[Auth flow »](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/auth-flow.md)** — bundled JWT flow (signup / activate / reset). Sessions only cover login/logout.
- **[Security »](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/security.md)** — `CSRFMiddleware` to harden POSTs against cross-site attacks even with `SameSite=lax`.
- **[Cache »](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/cache.md)** — `AsyncRedisManager` and `client_proxy`, the right handle for a middleware store like `RedisSessionStore`.

# Settings: composing the configuration mixins

Use this page to build the service's `Settings` class: which mixin brings each
environment variable, in which order to list the bases, and how to hand the
configuration to the SDK clients without copying field by field.

## Compose the `Settings` class

Use it when the service reads configuration from the environment (or from
`.env`): inherit the mixins you need and declare only what is yours.

```python
import asyncio
import logging

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    AsyncDatabaseManager,
    BaseAppSettings,
    DatabaseSettings,
    EnvironmentSettings,
    JWTSettings,
    JWTUtils,
    LogSettings,
    ServerSettings,
    UploadSettings,
    UploadUtils,
    configure_logging,
)


class Settings(
    EnvironmentSettings,
    ServerSettings,
    LogSettings,
    DatabaseSettings,
    JWTSettings,
    UploadSettings,
    BaseAppSettings,
):
    """Service configuration: six mixins and one field of its own."""

    SIGNUP_BONUS_POINTS: int = 100


settings: Settings = Settings()

logger: logging.Logger = configure_logging(**settings.logging_kwargs())
db: AsyncDatabaseManager = AsyncDatabaseManager(**settings.database_kwargs())
jwt: JWTUtils = JWTUtils(**settings.jwt_kwargs())
uploads: UploadUtils = UploadUtils(**settings.upload_kwargs())


async def main() -> None:
    """Connect to the database, issue a token and show what the environment set."""
    await db.connect()
    token: str = jwt.encode({"sub": "42"})
    print(settings.ENV, settings.SERVER_PORT, settings.SIGNUP_BONUS_POINTS)
    print(jwt.decode(token)["sub"], sorted(settings.UPLOAD_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS))
    await db.disconnect()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

The matching `.env.example` — copy it to `.env` and adjust:

```bash
# EnvironmentSettings: required. development, test or production.
ENV=development

# ServerSettings
SERVER_HOST=127.0.0.1
SERVER_PORT=8000
SERVER_RELOAD=false

# LogSettings
LOG_LEVEL=INFO
LOG_JSON=false
LOG_DIR=logs
LOG_REDACT=true

# DatabaseSettings
DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:///./app.db

# JWTSettings: generate the secret with
# python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"
JWT_SECRET=replace-with-a-secret-of-at-least-32-bytes
JWT_ACCESS_TTL_SECONDS=3600
# JWT_ISSUER=

# UploadSettings: lists are JSON.
UPLOAD_DIR=./var/uploads
UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE_BYTES=10485760
UPLOAD_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS=[".jpg", ".png", ".pdf"]
UPLOAD_ALLOWED_MIMETYPES=["image/jpeg", "image/png", "application/pdf"]

# The service's own field.
SIGNUP_BONUS_POINTS=100
```

Save the code as `settings_demo.py` next to the `.env`. With
`uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[auth,upload,sqlite]"`, `python settings_demo.py`
prints:

```text
development 8000 100
42 ['.jpg', '.pdf', '.png']
```

- Each mixin brings its own fields, with defaults and validation, plus the
  `*_kwargs()` mapper when there is a client to build; the service class only
  adds them up.
- `SIGNUP_BONUS_POINTS` is the field no mixin models — the only one declared
  by hand.
- A key with no value stays commented out (`# JWT_ISSUER=`): an empty `KEY=`
  fails the boot on a numeric field (`int_parsing`) and becomes `""`, not
  `None`, on a `str | None` field.

!!! tip "Do not redeclare a mixin field to change its default"

    Binding `0.0.0.0`, a bigger upload, JSON logs: those are environment
    values and belong in `.env`. Redeclaring `SERVER_HOST: str = "0.0.0.0"` in
    the class hides the real configuration from whoever reads `.env` and pins
    dev and production to the same value.

## List `BaseAppSettings` last

Apply this rule whenever you list `BaseAppSettings` next to the mixins: it
goes at the end of the base list.

Every mixin already inherits `BaseAppSettings`, and Python does not let a
class come before its own subclass in the base list. In the wrong order the
class is never created — the error is raised at import:

```python
# docs-guard: skip — this is the error described below
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, JWTSettings, ServerSettings


class Settings(BaseAppSettings, ServerSettings, JWTSettings):
    pass
```

```text
TypeError: Settings: BaseAppSettings must be the LAST base — ServerSettings
already subclasses it, so listing BaseAppSettings before it is an invalid
method resolution order (MRO). Move BaseAppSettings to the end of the base
list: class Settings(ServerSettings, BaseAppSettings).
```

Measured on 0.374.0 (Python 3.12.7, pydantic 2.13.5, pydantic-settings
2.15.0). With `BaseAppSettings` in the middle (`ServerSettings,
BaseAppSettings, JWTSettings`) the message is the same, naming `JWTSettings`.
Before v0.159.1 Python's raw `TypeError` came out (`Cannot create a consistent
method resolution order (MRO) for bases BaseAppSettings, ...`), with a
misleading `[metaclass]` error from mypy; the cause and the fix are the same.

Listing `BaseAppSettings` is optional: `class Settings(ServerSettings,
JWTSettings)` is created too and reads `.env`, because each mixin already
carries its `model_config`. Listing it last makes it explicit where the base
configuration comes from.

| What `BaseAppSettings` turns on | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `env_file=".env"` | reads `.env` from the current directory; an environment variable wins over the file |
| `extra="ignore"` | an unknown variable is ignored (a typo too) |
| `case_sensitive=True` | the variable name is the field name, exactly |
| `frozen=True` | `settings` is immutable once built |
| `hide_input_in_errors=True` | a validation error does not echo the environment into the log |

## Build clients with `*_kwargs()`

Use the mixin's mapper to build the client: the field → argument translation
lives in one place and the `TypedDict` lets mypy check the splat.

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import EmailSettings, EmailUtils


class Settings(EmailSettings):
    """E-mail only."""


settings: Settings = Settings()
mailer: EmailUtils = EmailUtils(**settings.email_kwargs())
```

`settings.email_kwargs()` returns `EmailKwargs`, with the STARTTLS ×
implicit TLS pair already resolved from `SMTP_USE_TLS`/`SMTP_USE_SSL`. The
`*_kwargs()` column of the table below names each mixin's mapper.

## Mixin table

Use it to find the mixin that models a variable and the extra its client
needs.

The 29 mixins of `tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings`, counted from `__all__` on
0.374.0. The mixin itself needs no extra — they all import with the base
install; the "Extra" column is what the **client** consuming the
configuration needs.

| Mixin | Extra | Main variables (total) | `*_kwargs()` → `TypedDict` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AuthSettings` | `[auth]` (`[mfa]`, `[webauthn]` optional) | `AUTH_SIGNUP_ENABLED`, `AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE`, `AUTH_TOKEN_DELIVERY`, `AUTH_MFA_ENABLED` (73) | — |
| `CORSSettings` | — | `CORS_ORIGINS`, `CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS`, `CORS_ALLOW_METHODS` (7) | — |
| `DatabaseSettings` | `[sqlite]` or `[postgres]` | `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_ECHO`, `DATABASE_POOL_SIZE` (8) | `database_kwargs()` → `DatabaseKwargs` |
| `EmailSettings` | `[email]` | `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_FROM_ADDR`, `SMTP_USE_TLS` (9) | `email_kwargs()` → `EmailKwargs` |
| `EnvironmentSettings` | — | `ENV` (1, required) | — |
| `FirebaseSettings` | `[firebase]` | `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, `FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH` (4) | `firebase_kwargs()` → `FirebaseKwargs` |
| `GenAISettings` | `[genai]` | `GENAI_CACHE_DIR`, `GENAI_OFFLINE`, `GENAI_HF_TOKEN` (3) | — |
| `GoogleDriveSettings` | `[google-drive]` | `GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID`, `GOOGLE_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS_PATH` (4) | `google_drive_kwargs()` → `GoogleDriveStorageKwargs` |
| `HostBridgeSettings` | — | `HOST_ALLOWED_BASE_PATHS`, `HOST_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` (5) | `hostbridge_kwargs()` → `HostBridgeKwargs` |
| `HostedGenAISettings` | `[genai-hosted]` | `GENAI_PROVIDER`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (16) | `anthropic_kwargs()` → `AnthropicKwargs`, `openai_kwargs()` → `OpenAIKwargs`, `openai_speech_kwargs()` → `OpenAISpeechKwargs`, `deepseek_kwargs()` → `DeepSeekKwargs`, `gemini_kwargs()` → `GeminiKwargs`, `hosted_kwargs()` → `HostedGenAIKwargs` |
| `JWTSettings` | `[auth]` | `JWT_SECRET`, `JWT_ALGORITHM`, `JWT_ACCESS_TTL_SECONDS` (5) | `jwt_kwargs()` → `JWTKwargs` |
| `KafkaSettings` | `[queue-kafka]` | `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS`, `KAFKA_SECURITY_PROTOCOL` (10) | `kafka_kwargs()` → `KafkaKwargs` |
| `LogSettings` | — | `LOG_LEVEL`, `LOG_JSON`, `LOG_DIR`, `LOG_REDACT` (8) | `logging_kwargs()` → `LoggingKwargs` |
| `MercadoPagoSettings` | `[http]` | `MERCADOPAGO_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `MERCADOPAGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (3) | `mercado_pago_kwargs()` → `HTTPClientKwargs` |
| `MinIOSettings` | `[minio]` | former name of `StorageSettings`; composing it emits a `DeprecationWarning` (20) | — |
| `OAuthSettings` | `[http]` | `OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE_URL`, `OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` (6) | `google_kwargs()` → `GoogleOAuthKwargs`, `github_kwargs()` → `GitHubOAuthKwargs` |
| `OpenPixSettings` | `[http]` | `OPENPIX_APP_ID`, `OPENPIX_ENVIRONMENT` (2) | `openpix_kwargs()` → `HTTPClientKwargs` |
| `PushSettings` | `[webpush]` + `[firebase]` | `WebPushSettings` + `FirebaseSettings` together (8) | — |
| `RabbitMQSettings` | `[queue]` | `RABBITMQ_URL`, `RABBITMQ_PREFETCH_COUNT` (2) | — |
| `RedisSettings` | `[cache]` | `REDIS_URL`, `REDIS_DECODE_RESPONSES` (2) | `redis_kwargs()` → `RedisKwargs` |
| `RevenueCatSettings` | `[http]` | `REVENUECAT_API_KEY`, `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (4) | `revenuecat_kwargs()` → `HTTPClientKwargs` |
| `ServerSettings` | — | `SERVER_HOST`, `SERVER_PORT`, `SERVER_RELOAD`, `TRUSTED_IP_HEADER` (7) | — |
| `SessionSettings` | — | `SESSION_TTL_SECONDS`, `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME`, `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` (9) | `session_cookie_kwargs()` → `SessionCookieKwargs`, `session_cookie_delete_kwargs()` → `SessionCookieDeleteKwargs` |
| `StorageSettings` | `[minio]` for `s3`; `local` needs none | `STORAGE_BACKEND`, `STORAGE_ENDPOINT`, `STORAGE_DEFAULT_BUCKET`, `STORAGE_LOCAL_DIR` (20) | `storage_kwargs()` → `StorageKwargs`, `minio_kwargs()` → `StorageKwargs`, `local_storage_kwargs()` → `LocalStorageKwargs` |
| `TaskIQSettings` | `[tasks]` or `[tasks-redis]` | `TASKIQ_BROKER_URL`, `TASKIQ_RESULT_BACKEND_URL` (7) | — |
| `TokenSettings` | — | `TOKEN_SECRET` (1) | — |
| `UploadSettings` | `[upload]` | `UPLOAD_DIR`, `UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE_BYTES`, `UPLOAD_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS` (4) | `upload_kwargs()` → `UploadKwargs` |
| `WebPushSettings` | `[webpush]` | `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`, `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`, `VAPID_SUBJECT` (4) | `webpush_kwargs()` → `WebPushKwargs` |
| `WebSocketSettings` | `[websocket]` | `WS_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS`, `WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_USER` (4) | — |

They all import from `tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings` and from the root too
(`from tempest_fastapi_sdk import JWTSettings`). The field name is the
environment variable name, with no prefix. The full field list, with defaults
and descriptions, is in the [reference](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/reference/top.md).

## Refuse development values in production

Use `EnvironmentSettings` so the boot fails when `ENV=production` still carries
a development default.

With the example at the top, `ENV=production` and the placeholder
`JWT_SECRET`:

```text
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Settings
  Value error, ENV=production refuses development values:
- DATABASE_URL: points at SQLite (the development default)
- JWT_SECRET: still the public placeholder declared by JWTSettings [type=value_error]
```

The guard only checks the mixins the class lists — each one declares what a
development value is for itself.

## Recap

- Inherit the mixins; declare by hand only the field no mixin models.
- `BaseAppSettings` is optional, but when it appears it goes **last** — in
  the wrong order, `TypeError` at import.
- Build clients with `Client(**settings.x_kwargs())`.
- Keep a `.env.example` with every key the service reads.
- Compose `EnvironmentSettings` so production refuses dev defaults.

Next steps: [Tutorial](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/tutorial.md#2-settings-server-app-factory-entry-point),
[Auth flow](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/auth-flow.md), [Uploads](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/uploads.md).

# Sharing with a preview (Open Graph)

When someone pastes a link into WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram or X, the
network fetches that URL and builds the preview (image, title and
description) from the **Open Graph** tags in the HTML it gets back. Those
crawlers **do not run JavaScript**: an SPA returns an empty `index.html`, and
the preview comes out blank.

So the **backend** answers the shared link. It returns, per item, a page with
the tags already in place and the preview image. `tempest_fastapi_sdk.share`
builds that from one function of yours that says what to show for each item.

By the end of this recipe you will have:

- `GET /s/{id}`: the HTML with `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`,
  `og:url`, `twitter:card` and `<link rel=canonical>`, with the human sent on
  to the app screen;
- `GET /s/{id}/og.png`: a 1200×630 card drawn with your brand, with `ETag` and
  `304`;
- a generic preview for an item that no longer exists, with no `500` and no
  leaked data.

## Installation

The page needs nothing beyond the base install. The PNG card uses Pillow,
which comes with the `[image]` extra:

```bash
uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[image]>=0.371.0"
```

The card also needs a TrueType font installed on the machine. On
Debian/Ubuntu that is the `fonts-dejavu-core` package. See
[Font in Docker](#font-in-docker).

## Step 1: the item page

You write **one** function: it gets the id from the URL and returns a
`SharePreviewSchema`, or `None` when the item must not be shown.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.share import SharePreviewSchema, make_share_router

TRIPS: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {
    "42": {"origin": "Teresina", "destination": "Fortaleza", "when": "Friday, 6pm"},
}


async def resolve_trip(item_id: str, /) -> SharePreviewSchema | None:
    trip = TRIPS.get(item_id)
    if trip is None:
        return None
    return SharePreviewSchema(
        title=f"Ride {trip['origin']} → {trip['destination']}",
        description=f"{trip['when']} · book your seat in the app",
        redirect_url=f"https://app.example.com/rides/{item_id}",
    )


app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(
    make_share_router(
        resolve_trip,
        public_url="https://api.example.com",
        fallback=SharePreviewSchema(
            title="BusCar",
            description="Rides between cities",
            redirect_url="https://app.example.com",
        ),
        site_name="BusCar",
        locale="en_US",
        link_text="Open in the app",
    )
)
```

Piece by piece:

- **`resolve_trip`** is the resolver. The `/` after `item_id` is not
  decoration: the router calls the resolver positionally, so the parameter
  name is yours to pick.
- **`redirect_url`** is where the **person** who clicks the link goes. The
  page sends the browser there with `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` and also
  shows a visible link (`link_text`) for when refresh is blocked. The default
  `link_text` is `"Open"`; pass your app's own wording (`"Open in the app"`,
  or `"Abrir no app"` in a pt-BR app).
- **`public_url`** is the public origin the link is served from. `og:url` and
  the image URL are built on it.
- **`fallback`** is the preview shown when the resolver returns `None`.
- **`site_name`** and **`locale`** are the same for every item, so they live
  on the router, not on the schema.

With the app running, `GET /s/42` returns:

```html
<title>Ride Teresina → Fortaleza</title>
<link rel="canonical" href="https://api.example.com/s/42">
<meta property="og:type" content="website">
<meta property="og:title" content="Ride Teresina → Fortaleza">
<meta property="og:description" content="Friday, 6pm · book your seat in the app">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://api.example.com/s/42">
<meta property="og:site_name" content="BusCar">
<meta property="og:locale" content="en_US">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary">
```

Both routes answer `GET` and `HEAD`, and stay **out of OpenAPI** by default. They are public pages, not
API. Pass `include_in_schema=True` to see them in `/docs`.

!!! warning "Why `public_url` is required"
    The router never builds a URL from `request.base_url`. Behind nginx that
    value is the internal address (`http://backend:8000`), and the `Host`
    header is the client's to choose. `og:image` must be absolute and public:
    the crawler has no page to resolve a relative path against, and an
    image it cannot find raises no error you would ever see.

### What is escaped, and what is refused

Every value that enters the HTML goes through `html.escape(..., quote=True)`:
title, description, alt text, `site_name`, `locale`, `link_text` and the
URLs. An item named `"><script>` becomes text, not code.

Escaping is not enough for a URL: `javascript:alert(1)` still runs inside
`href` after escaping. So `redirect_url`, `canonical_url` and `image_url`
only accept an **absolute** `http`/`https` URL. The schema refuses the rest
(`javascript:`, `data:`, `/path`, `//host`) with `ValidationError`, before
any HTML exists.

## Step 2: the unavailable item

When the resolver returns `None`, the page **still answers `200`**, with the
`fallback` text. `og:url` is still the shared link. A link someone sent before
the ride was cancelled opens the generic preview: it neither breaks nor tells
what the ride was.

Return `None` for anything that must not be shown: deleted, private, sold out
or another tenant's. An exception in the resolver does **not** become the
fallback: it propagates and becomes a `500`. A database outage is a failure,
not an "unavailable item", and swallowing it hides the problem.

## Step 3: the PNG card

Pass a `ShareCardRenderer` and fill `card` on the preview:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.share import (
    ShareCardLineSchema,
    ShareCardRenderer,
    ShareCardSchema,
    SharePreviewSchema,
    make_share_router,
)

TRIPS: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {
    "42": {
        "origin": "Teresina",
        "destination": "Fortaleza",
        "when": "Friday, 11/21 at 6pm",
        "stops": "Piripiri · Sobral",
        "price": "R$ 80 per seat",
        "seats": "3 seats",
        "driver": "Ana Souza (4.9)",
        "updated_at": "2026-11-20T14:03:00+00:00",
    },
}


async def resolve_trip(item_id: str, /) -> SharePreviewSchema | None:
    trip = TRIPS.get(item_id)
    if trip is None:
        return None
    route = f"{trip['origin']} → {trip['destination']}"
    return SharePreviewSchema(
        title=f"Ride {route}",
        description=f"{trip['when']} · {trip['price']}",
        redirect_url=f"https://app.example.com/rides/{item_id}",
        version=trip["updated_at"],
        card=ShareCardSchema(
            brand="BusCar",
            kicker="Ride available",
            title=route,
            lines=[
                ShareCardLineSchema(icon="→", text=f"Stops: {trip['stops']}"),
                ShareCardLineSchema(icon="★", text=trip["when"]),
            ],
            chips=[trip["price"], trip["seats"]],
            footer=f"Driver: {trip['driver']}",
        ),
    )


renderer = ShareCardRenderer(
    background=("#0b3d91", "#061f4a"),
    accent_color="#ffd166",
)

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(
    make_share_router(
        resolve_trip,
        public_url="https://api.example.com",
        fallback=SharePreviewSchema(
            title="BusCar",
            description="Rides between cities",
            redirect_url="https://app.example.com",
        ),
        renderer=renderer,
        site_name="BusCar",
        locale="en_US",
    )
)
```

Now the page gets `og:image` (with `og:image:width` 1200 and
`og:image:height` 630) and `twitter:card` becomes `summary_large_image`.
`GET /s/42/og.png` returns this (the Portuguese version of the same card):

![1200x630 share card with brand, route, stops, time, price and seat chips and the driver's name](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/assets/share-card.png)

The layout, top to bottom:

| Field | Where | When it does not fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | top, accent color | the font shrinks, then the text is cut with `…` |
| `kicker` | under the brand, muted color | the font shrinks, then the text is cut |
| `title` | bold, from 72 px down to 48 px on one line | the font shrinks to 48 px; if it still does not fit, wraps to two lines at 56 px, then is cut |
| `lines` | accent-colored icon + text | a line that does not fit above the chips is dropped |
| `chips` | rounded labels | a chip that would cross the margin is dropped |
| `footer` | bottom, muted color | the font shrinks, then the text is cut |

Every card text stays on one line: line breaks and repeated spaces become one
space (`"Friday\n6pm"` becomes `"Friday 6pm"`), and an empty chip is dropped.
A description typed with Enter does not bring the image down.

No text leaves the margin. The test
`tests/share/test_card.py::TestRender::test_long_text_stays_inside_margins`
pins that with 80 words in every field.

The renderer takes any color Pillow understands (`"#0b3d91"`,
`"rgb(11, 61, 145)"`, `"navy"`) and a `logo` (`bytes` or `Path`, PNG with
transparency), drawn at the top right, 72 px tall and at most 352 px wide (a
wider logo is scaled down until it fits). An invalid color, a logo
that is not an image and a missing font fail **at construction**, when the
service boots, not at the first share.

!!! tip "The icon is a character of the font"
    `icon` is drawn with the card's font. `→`, `★`, `✓` and `·` exist in
    DejaVu. A color emoji does not, and comes out as a box.

### Off the event loop

Drawing the card is CPU work: about 49 ms per card, the mean of 20
consecutive renders of a card with every field, on Pillow 13.0.0, on the
SDK's development machine (WSL2). The router calls `renderer.render` through
`asyncio.to_thread`, so the loop keeps serving other requests meanwhile. The
test `tests/share/test_router.py::TestEventLoop` checks that the render runs
on another thread, and fails if `to_thread` becomes a direct call.

## Step 4: cache, version and WhatsApp

Two cache layers are in play, and each asks for something different.

**The `ETag` avoids redrawing.** `og.png` answers with a weak `ETag` and
`Cache-Control: public, max-age=600` (change it with `cache_control=`). When
the client revalidates with `If-None-Match` and the tag matches, the answer
is `304` **without drawing anything**: one resolver call, no rendering. The
comparison follows RFC 9110 and accepts `W/"..."`, a list of tags and `*`.

The tag is derived from:

- the preview's `version` (your `updated_at`) or, without `version`, the
  `card` content;
- the renderer fingerprint (colors, fonts and logo): changing the brand color
  invalidates every card;
- the item id.

The tag is **weak** because two replicas with different FreeType builds can
produce different bytes for the same card. It promises "same content", not
"same bytes".

**The `?v=` makes the network fetch the new image.** The crawler keeps what
it fetched, keyed by URL. How long it keeps it, and whether it revalidates,
is each network's decision, outside your control. If the URL were always
`/s/42/og.png`, an edited ride could keep showing the old preview, `304` or
not. So the page publishes the image as `/s/42/og.png?v=<version hash>`. A
new `version` is a new URL, and to the network a different image.

!!! warning "Fill `version`"
    Without `version` the hash comes from the card content. That works, but
    the resolver builds the whole card on every revalidation. With
    `updated_at` in `version` the resolver can answer quickly, and the hash
    changes exactly when the item changes.

## Step 5: the public link, live

The link the driver shares is `https://<domain>/s/42`. Two ways to get that
path to the backend:

**nginx in front of the app and the API.** Forward the prefix to the backend
with `^~` and leave the rest to the SPA:

```nginx
location ^~ /s/ {
    proxy_pass http://backend:8000;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}

location ^~ /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://backend:8000;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}

location ~* \.(png|jpg|jpeg|gif|svg|ico|css|js|webp)$ {
    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    expires 7d;
}

location / {
    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    try_files $uri /index.html;
}
```

!!! danger "Without `^~`, the preview image disappears with no error"
    In nginx, a regex `location` (the static one, `~* \.(png|...)$`) beats a
    plain prefix such as `location /s/`. `/s/42/og.png` ends in `.png`, so it
    lands in the static block, which looks for the file on the SPA's disk and
    answers `404`. The `/s/42` page stays `200`, and the preview goes out
    without an image, with no error anywhere. `^~` tells nginx to stop at the
    prefix and skip the regexes. Measured on `nginx:alpine` 1.31.9 with this
    config: `location /s/` gave `404` on `og.png`, and `location ^~ /s/` gave
    `200 image/png`. Use `^~` on `/api/` too, where backend-generated images
    live (such as the [QR code](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/qr-logo.md)).

Here `public_url` is the app's domain (`https://app.example.com`), because
that is what appears in the link.

**The backend serves the SPA.** With
[`make_spa_router`](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/react-spa.md), include the share router **before** the
SPA. FastAPI matches routes in registration order, so `/s/{id}` matches
first. In the reverse order the SPA fallback answers `/s/42` with
`index.html`, and the preview comes out blank.

To check what the crawler sees, make the same request it makes:

```bash
curl -s https://app.example.com/s/42 | grep 'property="og:'
curl -sI https://app.example.com/s/42/og.png
```

To force a network to re-read a link already shared, use its tool. For
Facebook that is the
[Sharing Debugger](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/), with
"Scrape Again".

## Font in Docker

A `python:3.12-slim` image ships no TrueType font. Without one,
`ShareCardRenderer()` **does not start**:

```text
FileNotFoundError: no TrueType font found for the share card. Install one
(`apt-get install fonts-dejavu-core` on Debian/Ubuntu) or pass font_path= to
the renderer.
```

The SDK does not fall back to Pillow's bundled font on purpose. Measured on
Pillow 13.0.0, that font draws `ã` and `→` with the same box as a missing
character (`U+F0000`). A Portuguese preview would come out full of squares,
without any error.

Two ways out:

- install the font in the image. `tempest generate --dockerfile` already
  emits this line when the project pins the `[image]` extra:

    ```dockerfile
    RUN apt-get update \
        && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends fonts-dejavu-core \
        && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    ```

- or pass the file: `ShareCardRenderer(font_path=Path("fonts/Inter.ttf"),
  bold_font_path=Path("fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf"))`. An explicit path that does
  not exist is an error. The renderer does not look for another font in its
  place, because a typo there would make production draw with a font other
  than the one that was reviewed.

Without `font_path` the renderer looks, in order, for DejaVu on
Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora and Arch, then Liberation. The list is
`DEFAULT_FONT_CANDIDATES`.

## Just the page, no Pillow

Already have the image on a CDN? Do not pass `renderer` and fill `image_url`:

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.share import SharePreviewSchema


async def resolve_product(item_id: str, /) -> SharePreviewSchema | None:
    return SharePreviewSchema(
        title="Running shoes",
        description="US$ 59.90 · free shipping",
        redirect_url=f"https://shop.example.com/p/{item_id}",
        image_url=f"https://cdn.example.com/products/{item_id}.jpg",
    )
```

Without `renderer` the `og.png` route is not even registered, and the base
install is enough. `image_url` also works with a renderer: when set, it wins
over the generated card.

## Recap

- **`make_share_router(resolver, public_url=..., fallback=...)`** serves
  `GET /s/{id}` with the Open Graph and Twitter tags, all escaped, and sends
  the human on to `redirect_url`.
- **`SharePreviewSchema`** refuses any URL that is not absolute
  `http`/`https`. Escaping does not neutralize `javascript:`; refusing does.
- **The resolver returns `None`** for an unavailable item. The answer is
  `200` with the `fallback`, leaking nothing. An exception propagates as a
  `500`.
- **`ShareCardRenderer`** draws the 1200×630 card with your brand. Long text
  shrinks, wraps or is cut, and never leaves the margin. Without a font it
  fails at boot instead of drawing squares.
- **`version`** feeds the `ETag` (a `304` with no drawing) and the image's
  `?v=` (a new URL the network fetches again).
- **`public_url`** comes from configuration, never from the request's
  `Host`.

Source: https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/slides.md

# Slides, answer keys and Markdown to PDF

A service that teaches — or that asks a language model to put a lesson
together — ends up holding text like this:

```text
Lesson 1: Logic gates
What a gate is
A logic gate maps binary inputs to a single binary output.
```

And it has to deliver that as a presentation, as a PDF to print, as a
presenter handout. The usual path is one parser per format, each with its own
idea of what a bullet is, and the PowerPoint ends up saying one thing and the
PDF another.

`tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides` reads the text **once**, into a typed object, and
every format comes out of that same object: HTML, PDF, PPTX, DOCX and
Markdown. The same holds for answer keys (numbered questions and answers) and
for free-form Markdown turned into PDF, with the stylesheet you choose — ABNT
included.

!!! info "Required extra"
    ```bash
    uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[slides]"
    ```
    Brings in `weasyprint`, `jinja2`, `python-pptx`, `python-docx` and
    `markdown`. The PDF uses the same engine as
    [PDF generation](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/pdf.md), so it **needs the same system libraries** —
    read [Deployment](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/pdf.md#deployment-the-system-libraries). The parser and
    the schemas import without the extra: each engine loads on first use.

## Your first deck

```python
# scripts/lesson.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import SlideDeck, SlideRenderer, parse_slides

SOURCE: str = """Lesson 1: Logic gates
What a gate is
A logic gate maps binary inputs to a single binary output.
Notes: ask the class for a real-world example first.
The gates you will meet
- NOT gate: inverts its only input, so 0 becomes 1.
- AND gate: outputs 1 only when every input is 1.
- OR gate: outputs 1 when at least one input is 1.
Conclusion
Every digital circuit is built from a handful of gates.
"""


async def main() -> None:
    """Parse the lesson and write it as HTML and PowerPoint."""
    deck: SlideDeck = parse_slides(SOURCE)
    renderer = SlideRenderer()
    Path("lesson.html").write_text(renderer.html(deck), encoding="utf-8")
    Path("lesson.pptx").write_bytes(await renderer.pptx(deck))
    for slide in deck.slides:
        print(slide.slide_number, slide.kind, slide.title)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

Run it and you get:

```text
1 lesson_title Logic gates
2 content What a gate is
3 bullets The gates you will meet
4 conclusion Conclusion
```

Four slides, and every line of the text landed somewhere:

- **`Lesson 1: Logic gates`** opens a lesson and becomes its cover
  (`lesson_title`). The deck title, when you pass no `deck_title=`, is the
  first lesson's.
- **A short line (4 to 90 characters), capitalized, with no closing
  punctuation** (`What a gate is`) opens a section; a single word needs at
  least 8 characters, so a stray `Yes` does not open one. The section title is the slide title.
- **A paragraph** under a section becomes a content slide (`content`).
- **`Term: description`** becomes a bullet, and the bullets of a section share
  one slide (`bullets`). The leading dash is optional.
- **`Notes:`** is a speaker note, attached to the paragraph or bullet right
  above it.
- **A section whose title contains `conclusion`** becomes a conclusion slide.

`parse_slides` is synchronous: it is pure CPU over a string. The renderers
that produce binaries (`pdf`, `pptx`, `docx`) are `async` and run in a worker
thread, so a long deck does not block the event loop.

!!! tip "What does not become a bullet"
    A sentence with a colon in the middle would pass as a bullet if the rule
    were just "has a `:`". So the term must start with a capital, have at most
    8 words and 80 characters, carry no `.,!?;` and no unbalanced
    parenthesis, and contain no sentence verb (` is `, ` are `, ` means `, …);
    the description needs at least 20 characters. `The result is: 42 after
    the second pass.` stays a paragraph — without the full stop, the same
    line on its own becomes a section title.

### Slides that do not overflow

A section with a lot of content becomes more than one slide, instead of one
slide in a tiny font:

- **More than 6 bullets** open another slide with the same title. Measured
  with 8 bullets in a section: one slide with 6 and another with 2.
- **Paragraphs** group up to 700 characters per slide. A paragraph is never
  cut: one longer than the limit sits alone on its own slide.

## The vocabulary: text in your service's language

The markers the parser reads and the labels the renderers print are not
fixed. They live in a `SlideVocabulary`, English by default. A service that
writes Portuguese passes its own:

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import SlideDeck, SlideVocabulary, parse_slides

PT_BR: SlideVocabulary = SlideVocabulary(
    lesson_pattern=r"^Aula\s+(\d+)\s*:\s*(.+?)\s*$",
    notes_pattern=r"^(?:Notas|Nota)\s*:\s*(.+)$",
    conclusion_marker="conclus",
    sentence_verbs=(" é ", " são ", " foi ", " foram ", " será ", " tem ", " significa "),
    default_lesson_title="Conteúdo",
    lesson_label="Aula {index}",
    conclusion_label="Conclusão",
    handout_subtitle="Roteiro do apresentador",
    handout_cover_note="Slide de capa.",
    notes_heading="Notas do apresentador",
    language="pt-BR",
)

TEXT: str = """Aula 1: Portas lógicas
O que é uma porta
Uma porta lógica recebe entradas binárias e devolve uma única saída binária.
Notas: peça um exemplo do dia a dia antes de seguir.
As portas básicas
- Porta NOT: inverte a única entrada, então 0 vira 1.
- Porta AND: devolve 1 só quando todas as entradas valem 1.
Conclusão
Todo circuito digital é montado a partir de poucas portas.
"""

deck: SlideDeck = parse_slides(TEXT, vocabulary=PT_BR)
for slide in deck.slides:
    print(slide.slide_number, slide.kind, slide.title, slide.subtitle)
```

```text
1 lesson_title Portas lógicas Aula 1
2 content O que é uma porta None
3 bullets As portas básicas None
4 conclusion Conclusão None
```

Two parts, with different jobs:

- **Markers** (`lesson_pattern`, `notes_pattern`, `conclusion_marker`,
  `sentence_verbs`, `ignored_lines`) decide how the text is **read**. Both
  patterns are regular expressions, matched case-insensitively;
  `lesson_pattern` needs two groups (number and title), `notes_pattern` one
  (the note text). `conclusion_marker="conclus"` matches `Conclusão` and
  `Conclusões`.
- **Labels** (`lesson_label`, `conclusion_label`, `handout_subtitle`,
  `notes_heading`, `slide_label`, `language`, …) decide what is **printed**.
  `{index}` in `lesson_label` becomes the lesson number; `language` goes into
  `<html lang>`.

Without the vocabulary, the same Portuguese text comes out wrong — and with no
error at all, because nothing in it is invalid, it just is not what you meant.
Measured with the English default over the `TEXT` above:

```text
[('lesson_title', 'Content'), ('content', 'O que é uma porta'),
 ('bullets', 'O que é uma porta'), ('bullets', 'As portas básicas'),
 ('content', 'Conclusão')]
```

`Aula 1:` opened no lesson (the cover is the implicit `Content` one), the
`Notas:` line became a bullet and the conclusion became an ordinary slide.

!!! warning "Pass the same vocabulary to the renderer"
    ```python
    from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import SlideRenderer, SlideVocabulary

    PT_BR: SlideVocabulary = SlideVocabulary(
        lesson_pattern=r"^Aula\s+(\d+)\s*:\s*(.+?)\s*$",
        lesson_label="Aula {index}",
        conclusion_label="Conclusão",
    )
    renderer: SlideRenderer = SlideRenderer(vocabulary=PT_BR)
    ```
    The parser uses the markers; the renderer, the labels. A
    `SlideRenderer()` without a vocabulary prints `Lesson 1` and `Conclusion`
    on a deck read in Portuguese. Build the vocabulary once, as a service
    constant, and hand it to both.

An invalid pattern fails at **construction**, far from the first user text,
and the message names the field:

```text
ValueError: lesson_pattern needs two groups: number and title
ValueError: lesson_pattern is not a valid regular expression: missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 0
```

## Every format

One `SlideDeck`, five outputs:

| Format | Call | Speaker notes | Theme |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HTML | `renderer.html(deck, theme=...)` — sync, `str` | no | yes |
| PDF | `await renderer.pdf(deck, theme=...)` — `bytes` | no | yes |
| PPTX | `await renderer.pptx(deck, theme=...)` — `bytes` | in the notes pane | yes |
| DOCX | `await renderer.docx(deck)` — `bytes` | a block per page | no |
| Markdown | `renderer.markdown(deck)` — sync, `str` | a `Note:` block | no |

```python
# scripts/formats.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import SlideDeck, SlideRenderer, SlideThemeEnum, parse_slides


async def main() -> None:
    """Write one deck in every format."""
    deck: SlideDeck = parse_slides(Path("lesson.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    renderer = SlideRenderer(max_concurrent=2)
    Path("lesson.html").write_text(renderer.html(deck), encoding="utf-8")
    Path("lesson.md").write_text(renderer.markdown(deck), encoding="utf-8")
    Path("lesson.pdf").write_bytes(await renderer.pdf(deck, theme=SlideThemeEnum.DARK))
    Path("lesson.pptx").write_bytes(await renderer.pptx(deck, theme=SlideThemeEnum.DARK))
    Path("handout.docx").write_bytes(await renderer.docx(deck))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

What each one delivers, measured on the four-slide deck from the start:

- **HTML** is a single document, CSS inlined and nothing fetched — it opens
  offline and fits an `<iframe srcdoc>` preview. Every value is escaped.
- **PDF** is that same HTML laid out: one page per slide, 960 × 540 pt
  (1280 × 720 px). The four slides gave four pages.
- **PPTX** comes out 16:9 (13.33 × 7.5 inches), one slide per slide, with the
  speaker note in the notes pane — slide 2 carried
  `ask the class for a real-world example first.`, the others none.
- **DOCX** is the presenter handout: a cover with the title and
  `Presenter handout` (the `handout_subtitle`), then one page per slide with
  the lesson label, the title, the content and a `Speaker notes` block —
  holding the note, or blank lines to write on by hand. The footer reads
  `Logic gates  ·  Slide 1 / 4`.
- **Markdown** is reveal.js flavoured, slides separated by `---`:

```text
<!-- Deck: Logic gates -->
<!-- Total slides: 4 -->

<small>Lesson 1</small>

# Logic gates

---

<small>Lesson 1</small>

## What a gate is

A logic gate maps binary inputs to a single binary output.

Note:
ask the class for a real-world example first.
```

`SlideThemeEnum.DEFAULT` is dark text on white with blue accents;
`SlideThemeEnum.DARK`, light text on a slate background. `max_concurrent` caps
how many PDF, PPTX and DOCX renders run at once on that renderer — each is CPU
in a worker thread, and without a ceiling a burst of requests takes every
core.

## Answer keys

An answer key is another text format — title, parts, numbered questions and
answers — with its own parser and renderer:

```python
# scripts/answer_key.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import (
    AnswerKey,
    AnswerKeyRenderer,
    AnswerKeyVocabulary,
    parse_answer_key,
)

PT_BR: AnswerKeyVocabulary = AnswerKeyVocabulary(
    title_prefixes=("título:",),
    subtitle_prefixes=("subtítulo:",),
    answer_pattern=r"^(?:R|Resposta)\s*[:.]\s*(.*)$",
    default_title="Gabarito",
    answer_label="Resposta:",
    footer="Gabarito de uso do professor",
    language="pt-BR",
)

TEXT: str = """Título: Portas lógicas — gabarito
Subtítulo: Turma 3B, 2026

Parte 1: Conceitos
1. O que faz uma porta NOT?
R: Inverte a entrada: 0 vira 1 e 1 vira 0.
2. Quando a porta AND devolve 1?
Resposta:
Só quando <b>todas</b> as entradas valem 1.

Parte 2: Aplicação
1) Qual porta implementa "pelo menos um"?
R: A porta OR.
"""


async def main() -> None:
    """Parse the answer key and write it as Markdown, PDF and DOCX."""
    answer_key: AnswerKey = parse_answer_key(TEXT, vocabulary=PT_BR)
    renderer = AnswerKeyRenderer(vocabulary=PT_BR)
    print(answer_key.title, "|", answer_key.subtitle, "|", answer_key.total_items)
    Path("answer_key.md").write_text(renderer.markdown(answer_key), encoding="utf-8")
    Path("answer_key.pdf").write_bytes(await renderer.pdf(answer_key))
    Path("answer_key.docx").write_bytes(await renderer.docx(answer_key))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

```text
Portas lógicas — gabarito | Turma 3B, 2026 | 3
```

And `answer_key.md`:

```text
# Portas lógicas — gabarito

_Turma 3B, 2026_

## Parte 1: Conceitos

**1. O que faz uma porta NOT?**

> Resposta: Inverte a entrada: 0 vira 1 e 1 vira 0.

**2. Quando a porta AND devolve 1?**

> Resposta: Só quando todas as entradas valem 1.

## Parte 2: Aplicação

**1) Qual porta implementa "pelo menos um"?**

> Resposta: A porta OR.
```

The reading rules:

- **`1.` or `1)`** opens a question, and the numbering stays in its text.
- **The answer marker** (`answer_pattern`) opens the answer, which runs until
  the next question or part. The answer can start on the same line
  (`R: A porta OR.`) or on the next one (`Resposta:` alone) — several lines
  are joined with spaces.
- **A capitalized line that does not end like a sentence** opens a part — but
  only outside a question or after a blank line, so the second line of a
  wrapped question stays in the question.
- `title=` and `subtitle=` on the call override the lines in the text.

`AnswerKeyRenderer` has `html`, `markdown` (sync), `pdf` (A4) and `docx`
(`async`). `footer` prints one line at the end of the HTML and the PDF;
`None`, the default, prints none.

!!! note "HTML tags in the text are stripped, in every format"
    Answer keys written by a model sometimes arrive with `<b>`. The schema
    keeps the text as it came (`'Só quando <b>todas</b> as entradas valem
    1.'`), and every renderer strips the tag before writing — look at the
    Markdown above. The HTML then still escapes whatever is left. An answer
    `<script>alert(1)</script>yes` comes out `alert(1)yes`, as text, in all
    four formats.

## Markdown to PDF

The third job has no parser: free-form Markdown — a report, a thesis, a
document a model wrote — laid out as PDF. The stylesheet is a parameter:

```python
# scripts/thesis.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS, MarkdownPdf, MarkdownPdfRenderer

TEXT: str = """# Introdução

Este trabalho descreve as portas lógicas.

| Porta | Saída |
| --- | --- |
| NOT | inverte |
"""


async def main() -> None:
    """Render a Markdown document with the ABNT stylesheet."""
    renderer = MarkdownPdfRenderer(stylesheet=ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS)
    document: MarkdownPdf = await renderer.render(TEXT, title="TCC")
    Path(f"{document.title}.pdf").write_bytes(document.content)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

`render` returns a `MarkdownPdf` with `content` (the bytes) and `title` —
yours, or `default_title` (`"Document"`) when you pass none. Three possible
stylesheets:

- **`DEFAULT_MARKDOWN_CSS`** (the default): A4, sans-serif, page numbers.
- **`ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS`**: the ABNT NBR 14724 layout for Brazilian academic
  work — A4, 3 cm top and left margins and 2 cm bottom and right, Times New
  Roman 12 pt, 1.5 line spacing, justified text, 1.25 cm first-line indent,
  first-level headings in upper case. Measured: `# Introdução` comes out
  `INTRODUÇÃO` in the PDF text with this sheet, and `Introdução` with the
  default.
- **Yours**: any CSS the service maintains, passed as `stylesheet=`.

The Markdown enables tables, fenced code blocks, footnotes, a table of
contents (`toc`) and `attr_list`. Code is coloured when Pygments is installed
and left plain when it is not.

!!! danger "Raw text fetches nothing"
    Markdown from a user is a URL from a user: `![x](file:///etc/passwd)`
    would read the server's disk, and `![x](http://169.254.169.254/...)` would
    make a request from inside your network. `render` goes through the same
    [asset policy](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/pdf.md#security-what-a-template-may-load) as PDF
    generation, with nothing allowed: both raise `AssetRefused` (422,
    `PDF_ASSET_REFUSED`) and no PDF comes out. `data:` still passes, because
    it carries its own bytes — measured with an SVG image as
    `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...`.

### Markdown with images: the `.zip` archive

A document with an image has to bring the image along. `render_archive` takes
a `.zip` holding the Markdown and the files it references:

```python
# scripts/zipped_report.py

import asyncio
import io
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import MarkdownPdf, MarkdownPdfRenderer

SQUARE: str = (
    '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="10" height="10">'
    '<rect width="10" height="10"/></svg>'
)


def build_archive() -> bytes:
    """Zip one Markdown file and the image it references."""
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buffer, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
        archive.writestr("report/report.md", "# With an image\n\n![square](img/q.svg)\n")
        archive.writestr("report/img/q.svg", SQUARE)
    return buffer.getvalue()


async def main() -> None:
    """Render a zipped Markdown document with its image."""
    document: MarkdownPdf = await MarkdownPdfRenderer().render_archive(build_archive())
    print(document.title)
    Path(f"{document.title}.pdf").write_bytes(document.content)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

It prints `report`: without `title=`, the title is the Markdown file's name
without its extension. How the file is chosen and what it may read:

- **The first `.md` in path order** is the document. With `a.md` and `b.md`
  in the same zip, `a.md` wins.
- **Relative paths resolve from the Markdown's directory** — `img/q.svg`
  above is `report/img/q.svg`.
- **Nothing outside the extracted zip can be read.**
  `![x](../../../../etc/passwd)` raises `AssetRefused`: that render's asset
  policy allows only the extraction directory.

And the archive is checked **before** a single byte reaches the disk, from
the zip's central directory. Each refusal is a `MarkdownArchiveError` (422,
`MARKDOWN_ARCHIVE_INVALID`) with `details["reason"]`:

| `reason` | When |
| --- | --- |
| `not_a_zip` | the bytes are not a zip |
| `unsafe_member` | an entry would land outside the extraction directory (`../outside.md`, `/abs.md`) |
| `too_many_members` | more entries than `max_archive_members` (default `DEFAULT_MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS`, 500) |
| `too_large` | the declared uncompressed size exceeds `max_archive_bytes` (default `DEFAULT_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES`, 50 MiB) |
| `no_markdown` | no `.md` in the zip |
| `not_utf8` | the Markdown is not UTF-8 |

`too_large` is what holds a zip bomb back: measured, a 221-byte zip declaring
100,000 uncompressed bytes is refused with `max_archive_bytes=50_000`,
without extracting. The refused entry's name never goes into the error — it
is text chosen by whoever sent the file.

### Mermaid diagrams

WeasyPrint runs no JavaScript, so a `` ```mermaid `` block would reach the PDF
as code. With `render_mermaid=True`, each block is drawn in headless Chromium
before layout:

```bash
uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[slides,slides-mermaid]"
uv run playwright install chromium
```

```python
# scripts/flow.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import MarkdownPdf, MarkdownPdfRenderer

FENCE: str = "`" * 3
TEXT: str = f"# Flow\n\n{FENCE}mermaid\ngraph TD\n  Order-->Payment\n{FENCE}\n"


async def main() -> None:
    """Render a document whose Mermaid block becomes a drawing."""
    renderer = MarkdownPdfRenderer(
        mermaid_timeout=15.0,
        mermaid_error_message="This diagram could not be drawn.",
    )
    document: MarkdownPdf = await renderer.render(TEXT, render_mermaid=True)
    Path("flow.pdf").write_bytes(document.content)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

Measured with Chromium installed: the valid diagram becomes inline SVG (its
node labels show up in the PDF text), and an invalid block in the same
document becomes a box with the message and the escaped source. One browser
draws every block of the document.

A failing diagram never takes the document down. Without Playwright, without
Chromium (measured with Playwright installed and the browser missing), with
invalid syntax or past the deadline (measured with `mermaid_timeout=0.001`),
the block becomes the `.mermaid-error` box and the PDF still comes out. Both
stylesheets the SDK ships style that box and `.mermaid-diagram`; a sheet of
your own that starts from either keeps diagrams inside the page.

!!! warning "The Mermaid script comes from the internet"
    The Chromium page loads `mermaid@10.9.8` from jsDelivr on every render.
    That request is the browser's, **outside** the PDF's asset policy — the
    server needs egress to `cdn.jsdelivr.net`. Measured by pointing the
    script at an address that does not answer: the diagram becomes an error
    box. The version is pinned, so a new Mermaid release does not change your
    PDF without notice.

!!! info "Why it is a separate extra, and out of `[all]`"
    Playwright asks for a browser download (`playwright install chromium`)
    that a service rendering plain decks should not carry. That is why
    `[slides-mermaid]` is neither in `[slides]` nor in `[all]`.

## Errors

They are all `AppException`s: let them propagate from the route and the
client gets the SDK envelope, with `code`. With
`register_exception_handlers(app, catalog=default_message_catalog())`, the
sentence follows `Accept-Language` — entries exist in pt-BR and en-US.

| Exception | Status | `code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SlideSourceEmptyError` | 422 | `SLIDES_SOURCE_EMPTY` | empty or whitespace text (parser, `render`, empty Markdown in a zip) |
| `SlideSourceTooLargeError` | 413 | `SLIDES_SOURCE_TOO_LARGE` | text longer than `max_chars` (default `DEFAULT_MAX_SOURCE_CHARS`, 200,000); `details={"limit": n}` |
| `MarkdownArchiveError` | 422 | `MARKDOWN_ARCHIVE_INVALID` | archive refused; `details={"reason": ...}`, table above |
| `AssetRefused` | 422 | `PDF_ASSET_REFUSED` | the Markdown referenced something not allowed; `details={"refused_count": n}` |

`max_chars=None` on `parse_slides`, `parse_answer_key` or the
`MarkdownPdfRenderer` disables the limit. None of these errors echoes the
