# Migration 0.34x–0.35x

Use when upgrading from a version older than these releases: 0.353.0, 0.349.0, 0.344.0, 0.343.0, 0.342.0, 0.341.0 and 0.340.0.

Part of the [Migration guide](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/migration.md).

## 0.353.0 — Gemini's `google_kwargs()` becomes `gemini_kwargs()`

`HostedGenAISettings.google_kwargs()` (Gemini) and `OAuthSettings.google_kwargs(prefix=...)` (Google login) shared a name. A `Settings` composing both kept the first one in the MRO, and Google login broke with `TypeError` on `prefix`. The Gemini one was renamed, with no alias (an alias would keep the clash).

| Where | What changes | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HostedGenAISettings` | `google_kwargs()` is now `gemini_kwargs()`; same return value, same `ValueError` when `GOOGLE_MODEL` is empty | `OpenAICompatGenerator(**settings.google_kwargs())` becomes `OpenAICompatGenerator(**settings.gemini_kwargs())`. With the old name, a `Settings` with only `HostedGenAISettings` raises `AttributeError` |
| `OAuthSettings` | **Nothing**: `google_kwargs(prefix=...)` is still the Google login one | Nothing; services composing both mixins now get the right method |
| `WebPushSettings` / `FirebaseSettings` | `enabled` becomes `webpush_enabled` and `firebase_enabled`, with no alias. Both had the same name and different meanings, and a `Settings` composing both without `PushSettings` read the answer of the first one in the MRO (#742) | `settings.enabled` on a service with `WebPushSettings` becomes `settings.webpush_enabled`; with `FirebaseSettings`, `settings.firebase_enabled`. The old name raises `AttributeError`. `PushSettings.enabled`, `web_enabled` and `mobile_enabled` **do not change** |

## 0.349.0 — Coqui in its own extra, oversized upload as 413 and a stricter `tempest check`

| Where | What changes | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[genai-audio]` | No longer brings `coqui-tts`, `torchaudio`, `torchcodec` or `six`: `TextToSpeech` (XTTS) moves to the new `[genai-tts-coqui]` extra. `SpeechToText` is unchanged | If you use `TextToSpeech`, install `[genai-audio,genai-tts-coqui]` (or just `[genai-tts-coqui]`, without STT). Otherwise the first synthesis raises `ImportError` naming `[genai-tts-coqui]` |
| `read_upload_capped` and the routes that use it (`make_genai_router`'s `/transcribe`, `make_voice_router`, `make_vision_router`) | An upload over the ceiling raises `UploadTooLargeException` (`413`, `code` `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE`) instead of `ValidationException` (`422`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`). `detail` and `details.max_bytes` are unchanged | A client that handled the size `422` handles `413` instead. A service that caught `ValidationException` to re-raise as `413` can drop the wrapper; `except FileTooLargeException` also catches the new exception |
| `tempest check` | Runs two new steps between `mypy` and `pytest`: `openapi-errors` (the same `--check`, which also fails on a declared but unreachable exception) and `lint-schemas`. And `openapi-errors` now follows FastAPI dependencies, so a route whose router requires `require_token` or whose provider answers 404 reports what it did not declare | Run `tempest openapi-errors --check` and `tempest lint-schemas` and fix; `tempest openapi-errors --fix` writes the missing declarations. To migrate gradually, `check_openapi_errors = false` / `check_lint_schemas = false` under `[tool.tempest]` |

## 0.344.0 — token of a deleted account

| Where | What changes | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `UserAuthService.current_user_dependency` | A valid token of a deleted account (or a `sub` that is not a UUID) answers `401 UNAUTHORIZED` instead of `404 NOT_FOUND`; with `soft=True`, the dependency yields `None` | Nothing, if the client already treats `401` as session over. Whoever handled the `404` of those routes switches to `401`; whoever reimplemented the loader just to translate the `404` can go back to `current_user_dependency()` |

## 0.343.0 — every SDK enum ends in `Enum`

Eighty hand-written public enums gained the suffix the others already had
(`PdfExtractor` → `PdfExtractorEnum`, `JobStatus` → `JobStatusEnum`,
`UF` → `UFEnum`). There is no alias: the old name is gone, and the import
fails immediately.

```text
ImportError: cannot import name 'JobStatus' from 'tempest_fastapi_sdk.tasks'
```

| Where | What changes | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `import` and type annotations | The old name no longer exists | Use the new name from the table below; your editor's symbol rename (not a text replace) keeps "UF" or "Locale" in prose intact |
| Your service's OpenAPI | The component carries the class name: `JobStatus` becomes `JobStatusEnum` | Regenerate the frontend client; anything referencing `#/components/schemas/JobStatus` by hand updates the reference |
| Serialized value (JSON, database) | **Nothing**: `JobStatusEnum.QUEUED` is still `"queued"` | Nothing |
| Native Postgres type | **Nothing**: `TempestEnum` and `enum_column` drop one trailing `Enum` before naming the type, so `JobStatus` and `JobStatusEnum` both yield `job_status_enum` (measured on all 80) | Nothing; no migration is generated |

Enums generated from a provider's specification (OpenPix, Mercado Pago,
zap-api, `StripeEvent`) keep the specification's name.

## 0.342.0 — required `ENV` and empty `X-Token` secret

| Where | What changes | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EnvironmentSettings.ENV` | **No default** (was `development`): settings composing the mixin with no `ENV` in the environment or the `.env` raise `ValidationError` (`ENV Field required`) at boot | Set `ENV` in every environment — dev `.env`, container, CI, worker, migration job. In `conftest.py`, `os.environ["ENV"] = "test"` before importing the app |

| `make_token_dependency`, `require_x_token` | An empty (or whitespace-only) secret raises `ValueError` instead of disabling the check | Configure the secret (`tempest secrets init`); for a local run without the gate, pass `allow_unauthenticated=True`. # Migration 0.33x

Use when upgrading from a version older than these releases: 0.336.0, 0.335.0, 0.332.0, 0.331.0 and 0.330.0.

## 0.336.0 — security fixes (real time)

| Where | What changes | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SSEBroker` with Redis | With the default `channel_prefix` `"sse"`, construction logs a `WARNING`: Redis pub/sub ignores the DB index, and another service on the same instance with the same prefix exchanges events with this one | Pass a service-specific `channel_prefix` (`"orders-api:sse"`) on every worker at once — workers with different prefixes do not see each other |
| Web Push subscription (`WebPushSubscriptionService.subscribe`, `make_web_push_router`, `web` registration on `make_push_router`) | An endpoint that is or resolves to a non-public address answers `422 PUSH_ENDPOINT_NOT_PUBLIC` and is not stored; `send_many` returns for pruning a previously stored endpoint that is not `https` or whose host is a non-public IP literal | Nothing, if the push service is public. Self-hosted push service on the internal network: `allow_private_networks=True` on the `WebPushDispatcher` opens subscription and delivery together |

## 0.336.0 — `password-change` returns a fresh pair, `set-password` deletes passkeys

| Where | What changes | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /auth/password-change` | Answers **200** with `LoginResponseSchema` instead of `204` with no body, and the body takes an optional `code`. Account without MFA: a fresh pair, issued after every session is revoked (in cookies for a caller that authenticated with the access cookie). Account with MFA and no `code`: the password changes and the response is the login challenge (`mfa_required: true`, `mfa_token`), with no pair. With a valid `code`: a pair with an MFA `amr`; a wrong `code`: **401** and nothing changes | Bearer client: store the response's pair and drop the old one; on an MFA account, send the `code` along or handle `mfa_required` as at login. A client that treated any `2xx` as success does not break, but still gets signed out when the access token's TTL ends unless it stores the pair |
| `tempest user set-password` | Deletes the user's WebAuthn passkeys in the same transaction when it finds the table (`--webauthn-credential-model`, default `src.db.models:UserWebAuthnCredentialModel`) | `--keep-passkeys` keeps the old behaviour; tell the user they register their passkey again |
| `signup(fields=...)` and `signup_schema` | `totp_secret`, `totp_enabled_at`, `totp_last_step` and every `__secret_columns__` column of the user model are refused (`ValueError` in the service, dropped by the route) | Nothing for the MFA columns, which only the enrollment flow writes. If your signup writes a `__secret_columns__` column of your own, move that write to `on_signup` |
| `IntrospectionAuth` | New `audiences=`; without it, one `WARNING` per instance at construction | Pass `audiences=` with the service's client id at the provider. See [Bind the token to this service](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/introspection-auth.md#bind-the-token-to-this-service-audiences) |

## 0.336.0 — CORS, storage, text search and Stripe

| Where | What changes | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CORSSettings` with `ENV=production` | With `CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS=true`, `"null"` in `CORS_ORIGINS` or a `CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX` that matches a `.invalid` origin (`.*`, `https://.*`) stop the boot, as `"*"` already did | List the frontend origins in `CORS_ORIGINS`, or anchor the regex to your domain |
| `accel_redirect_response`, `serve_object(accel_redirect=True)` | A `media_type` outside `type/subtype` (parameter, comma, CR/LF) raises `ValueError`, as in `presigned_get_url`; `text/plain; charset=utf-8` is no longer accepted on this path | Pass the type without parameters (`text/plain`) |
| Text search (`search`, `search_condition`, `full_text_search`) | `hashed_password` and the `__secret_columns__` answer `422`; the message becomes `... has no searchable column ...`, and `details["allowed"]` only appears when the repository declares `searchable_columns` | If the search takes the field from the request, declare `searchable_columns` on the repository |
| `StripeClient` | `create`, `retrieve`, `update` and `delete` raise `StripeObjectMismatchError` when the response's `object` is not the resource's | Handle it where you handle `StripeError` today (it is a subclass) |
| `ps_single_quote` (hostbridge) | Also doubles the typographic quotes U+2018–U+201B | Nothing |

## 0.335.0 — `BaseUserModel` gains the `email_verified_at` column

`BaseUserModel` now maps `email_verified_at` (timezone-aware timestamp,
nullable): **when** the account holder proved they read the current address.
Since the column is mapped on the base, **migrate the database before upgrading
the package**: without it, every query on the user model fails (`no such
column: users.email_verified_at`, measured with SQLite).

The behaviour change: social login's link by email
(`AUTH_OAUTH_LINK_BY_VERIFIED_EMAIL=true`) now requires the column to be set.
An existing account has `NULL`, so it **stops being linked by email** (`409
OAUTH_EMAIL_TAKEN`) until it proves the address — through
`POST /auth/email-verify/request` and the link that arrives in the mailbox. A
service with the knob off (the default) changes nothing beyond the migration.
What sets and what clears the column is in
[What counts as a verified email](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/auth-flow/email-change.md#what-counts-as-a-verified-email).

### What to do

1. Generate the migration (`uv run tempest db revision -m "email verified at"`,
   or `alembic revision --autogenerate`) or write it by hand:

    ```python
    import sqlalchemy as sa
    from alembic import op

    revision: str = "email_verified_at"
    down_revision: str | None = "<the previous revision>"


    def upgrade() -> None:
        """Add the proof of email ownership."""
        op.add_column(
            "users",
            sa.Column("email_verified_at", sa.TIMESTAMP(timezone=True), nullable=True),
        )


    def downgrade() -> None:
        """Drop the proof of email ownership."""
        op.drop_column("users", "email_verified_at")
    ```

2. Run `uv run tempest db upgrade` (or `alembic upgrade head`) and only then
   deploy the new version.

### Backfilling existing accounts — your decision

The SDK fills nothing for you: it does not know how each existing account
became active. Backfill only if you **know** the active accounts in the
database were activated through the mailed link — that is, the service always
ran with `AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE=false`, `AUTH_RETURN_TOKEN_IN_RESPONSE=false` and
`EmailUtils` wired, and nobody activated an account from the admin site or
through `tempest user activate`. If any of that failed for part of the
database, narrow the `WHERE` to the rest (by `created_at`, for instance) or do
not backfill.

There is no column holding the activation time; `created_at` is the lower
bound the database knows, and it is the value the step below writes. Add to
the migration's `upgrade()`:

```python
import sqlalchemy as sa
from alembic import op


def upgrade() -> None:
    """Mark the active accounts, activated by email, as verified."""
    users = sa.table(
        "users",
        sa.column("is_active", sa.Boolean()),
        sa.column("created_at", sa.TIMESTAMP(timezone=True)),
        sa.column("email_verified_at", sa.TIMESTAMP(timezone=True)),
    )
    op.execute(
        users.update()
        .where(users.c.is_active.is_(True), users.c.email_verified_at.is_(None))
        .values(email_verified_at=users.c.created_at)
    )
```

Without this step, an account that wants to link social login by email
verifies its address once, and linking works again.

## 0.335.0 — security fixes that change behaviour

This release closes vulnerabilities, and several fixes swap an unsafe default
for a safe one. The table says what changes for existing users of the SDK and
what to do. Each item is detailed in the CHANGELOG and in the recipe named.

| Where | What changes | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ENV=production` | `AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE=true` or `AUTH_RETURN_TOKEN_IN_RESPONSE=true` stop the boot; without `EmailUtils` on `UserAuthService` (with an `auth_settings` that composes `EnvironmentSettings`), the flows that send a link answer `503 INTEGRATION_DISABLED` | Turn both flags off in production and pass `email=` to the service |
| `key_by_header` | `is_known=` is required; without it, `TypeError` | Pass a synchronous check that says whether the header value is a key you issued |
| `IdempotencyMiddleware` | Requests without a credential are not deduplicated; entries written by an older version answer `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` until they expire | Pass `allow_anonymous=True` only if you need to deduplicate anonymous `POST`s; wait out the TTL of old entries |
| `WebhookSignatureVerifier`, `make_stripe_webhook_dependency` | An empty secret raises `ValueError` at construction | Configure the webhook secret before booting |
| `POST /auth/webauthn/register/begin` | Requires a `WebAuthnRegisterBeginSchema` body (`current_password` and, with MFA, `code`); without it, `422` | Update the client to ask for the password before registering a passkey |
| Password reset and `mfa_reset` | Delete the user's passkeys | `revoke_passkeys=False` keeps the old behaviour; tell users they register their passkey again |
| `make_admin_router` with `access_policy` | The SQL console, tasks and logs are denied to everyone | Pass `surface_policy=` granting whoever should see them |
| Admin | The SDK's credential columns (`totp_secret`, push keys, token digests) disappear from the screens, `list_display` included; cookies issued before the upgrade are refused once | Nothing; operators log in again |
| Custom `SessionStore` | The protocol gained `touch`; a store without it works with a `DeprecationWarning` | Implement `touch`, which updates only a session that still exists |
| `TaskQueue` (results) | Results are stored as JSON; pickled results from before the upgrade are unreadable until their TTL | `result_serializer="pickle"` only for a Redis nobody else writes |
| `WebPushDispatcher` | Endpoints resolving to an internal network are not delivered; sending has a 10 s timeout | `allow_private_networks=True` only in test environments; behind a proxy with no external DNS, pass `resolver=` |
| `describe_image_tool`, `transcribe_audio_tool` | The `path` argument exists only with `path_root=` | Pass `path_root=` with the folder the model may read |
| `ChatMemory.delete_for_chat` | Requires `user_id` | Pass the chat's owner |
| `HoneypotMiddleware` | `patterns=` matches the path only; the query has `query_patterns=` | Move query patterns to `query_patterns=` |
| STT, diarization, voiceprint | Audio longer than 1 h once decoded is refused (`422`) | `max_audio_seconds=None` for trusted long files |
| WebSocket login | Use `make_jwt_bearer_resolver`, which checks the token type | Replace the hand-written resolver |

## 0.332.0 — the DLQ pins the consumer's ack policy

On a `QueueSpec` with a dead-letter, `MessageBroker.on` / `register` and
`subscribe` / `Consumer` pin `REJECT_ON_ERROR` on the subscriber itself when
`ack_policy` is `None` (#642). Passing `ACK`, `ACK_FIRST` or `NACK_ON_ERROR`
on a dead-lettered spec now raises `ValueError` at registration: none of the
three sends the failure to the DLQ. A consumer without a dead-letter is
unchanged.

### What to do

1. Drop `ack_policy=AckPolicy.REJECT_ON_ERROR` from dead-lettered consumers
   if you like: it is now the default. Keeping it still works.
2. A dead-lettered consumer that passed `ACK`, `ACK_FIRST` or
   `NACK_ON_ERROR` fails at boot: switch to `REJECT_ON_ERROR` (or omit it), or
   drop the dead-letter from the spec if failures should not go to the DLQ.

## 0.331.0 — new admin look, capped storage uploads

`admin.css` was rewritten on tokens and `AdminTheme` changed two defaults:
`header_bg` goes from `"#0f172a"` to `"#ffffff"` and `radius` from `"6px"`
to `"8px"`. The `tempest-admin-*` classes stay.

The `SubjectStorageClient` protocol gained `presigned_post_policy`, and
`presigned_get_url` gained `filename`, `media_type` and `as_attachment`.

The admin list search (`?q=`) now matches a substring in any of the
`search_fields`; it used to compare by equality in all of them.

### What to do

1. If you pass `custom_css_url` overriding fixed colors of the dark header:
   review the sheet against the light header.
2. To keep a dark header, pass `AdminTheme(header_bg="#0f172a")`: the chrome
   text turns light on its own from the luminance. If the guess is wrong,
   pin it with `header_fg=`.
3. Behind a proxy that terminates TLS, use the upgrade to declare
   `SERVER_PUBLIC_SCHEME=https` and register the `PublicSchemeMiddleware`
   ([Security](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/security.md#public-scheme-behind-a-proxy-server_public_scheme)):
   without it the admin login shows as not secure.
4. A storage client of yours implementing `SubjectStorageClient` needs
   `presigned_post_policy` and the three new `presigned_get_url` parameters
   to keep passing the type-checker. `AsyncMinIOClient`,
   `LocalObjectStorageClient` and `FakeObjectStorageClient` already comply.
5. A service that generates a client from the OpenAPI and uses
   `image_media_type_field`: call `prune_orphan_enum_schemas(app)` in
   `create_app` to drop the orphan `ImageMediaType`
   ([Uploads](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/uploads.md)).

## 0.330.0 — a push subscription no longer changes owner

`POST /subscribe` (Web Push) and `POST /register` (mobile push) no longer
transfer to the caller an `endpoint`/`token` already registered by another
account (#632): the row stays with its owner and the route answers as for a
new subscription. Before, another account signing in on the same browser or
device moved the subscription on its own.

### What to do

1. In the client, call `POST /unsubscribe` (Web Push) or `POST /unregister`
   (mobile) on **sign-out**, before another account uses the same device.
2. If moving devices between accounts is a real case for your service, turn
   it on explicitly: `make_web_push_router(..., transfer_ownership=True)` /
   `make_push_router(..., transfer_ownership=True)`, or
   `subscribe(..., transfer_ownership=True)` /
   `register(..., transfer_ownership=True)` on the service.
3. A `subscribe`/`register` override does not need to change: the router
   passes `transfer_ownership` only when the option is on.

# Migration 0.32x

Use when upgrading from a version older than these releases: 0.327.0, 0.325.0, 0.323.0, 0.322.0, 0.321.0 and 0.320.0.

Part of the [Migration guide](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/migration.md).

## 0.327.0 — the #616 architecture rules, as warnings

Nothing changes in the code you already have: the new `tempest check` rules
(`LAY*`, `IMP*`, `DI*`, `REPO002`, `RTR003`/`RTR004`, `STR*`, `TST*`) enter as
**warnings** and fail the gate only with `layers_strict = true`.

### What to do

1. Run `tempest lint-layers` and count the warnings per code.
2. Follow the order and the traps in
   [Recommended architecture › Migrating an existing service](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recommended-architecture.md#migrating-an-existing-service),
   one family per PR, with `tempest lint-layers --rule <CODE>`.
3. Once a family reaches zero, turn on `layers_strict = true` under
   `[tool.tempest]`.

## 0.325.0 — CSRF on the admin login and the `[cli-ops]` extra

`POST /admin/login` now requires the `csrf_token` that `GET /admin/login`
issues. The CLI gains the `[cli-ops]` extra, without the quality gate.

### What to do

- A test that signs in to the admin by posting only the credentials
  (`client.post("/admin/login", data={"identifier": ..., "password": ...})`)
  now gets `403`. Switch to `tempest_fastapi_sdk.testing.admin_login`
  (async) or `admin_login_sync` (`TestClient`), which load the form and send
  the token. With `cookie_secure=True`, give the client
  `base_url="https://..."`: the token cookie is `Secure`.
- An admin served over plain HTTP with `cookie_secure=True` (which already
  could not keep a session) now refuses every login with `403` "The sign-in
  form expired". The fix is the same as before: HTTPS in front, or
  `cookie_secure=False`.
- Code that read `tempest_fastapi_sdk.cli.main.LINT_LAYERS_STEP` must handle
  `None` (without `tempest-cli` installed). `find_pyproject`, from
  `tempest_fastapi_sdk.cli.config`, is now the SDK's own; the other config
  names stay importable from the same place.
- Optional: `tempest` in production can swap `[cli]` for `[cli-ops]`, which
  installs neither `ruff` nor `tempest-cli`. Keep `[cli]` in the `dev` group.

## 0.323.0 — the dead-letter topology comes up before the consumers

On RabbitMQ, `MessageBroker.connect()` now opens the connection, runs
`declare_topology()` and only then starts the consumers. The declaration used
to come after, and a message rejected in that window was lost.

### What to do

- A queue that already exists on the broker with arguments other than the
  `QueueSpec`'s (a DLQ created by hand with another `x-queue-type` or with
  `x-message-ttl`) makes `connect()` fail with `PRECONDITION_FAILED -
  inequivalent arg ...` before any consumer runs. Align the `QueueSpec` with
  what exists, delete the queue, or pass `declare_topology=False` and manage
  the topology outside.
- `publish(..., exchange=...)` is now a named parameter and the channel becomes
  the routing key: passing `routing_key=` alongside through `**options` raises
  `ValueError` — pass the key as the channel.

## 0.322.0 — SMTP failure becomes `503 EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE` and the guard checks TLS × port

`EmailUtils.send` and `send_many` now raise `EmailDeliveryException`
(`503`, `code="EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE"`) on every transport failure instead of the
`aiosmtplib` error. With `ENV=production` and e-mail enabled,
`EmailSettings` refuses a TLS mode that does not match the port.

### What to do

- Code that caught `aiosmtplib.SMTPException` (or `OSError`) around a send:
  catch `EmailDeliveryException` (exported at the package top level). A
  network or TLS failure carries the original error in `__cause__`; a refusal
  answered by the server is raised `from None`.
- Check `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USE_TLS` and `SMTP_USE_SSL` before deploying to
  production: `587` needs `SMTP_USE_TLS=true` and `SMTP_USE_SSL=false`;
  `465` needs `SMTP_USE_SSL=true` and `SMTP_USE_TLS=false`. Both enabled
  also fails the boot.
- `make_auth_router` clients: `/signup`, `/email-change/*`,
  `/email-verify/request` and `/email-recovery/request` may answer
  `503 EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE` (nothing stored; safe to retry).
  `/activation/request` and `/password-reset/request` keep their usual
  `202`.

## 0.321.0 — `SubjectStorageClient` gains three methods

The `SubjectStorageClient` protocol (the type of `SubjectObjectStorage.client`)
now declares `presigned_put_url`, `stat_object` and `stream_object`, which
`SubjectObjectStorage` uses for direct upload (`presign_put`, `stat`, `read`).
`AsyncMinIOClient` and `FakeObjectStorageClient` already implement all three.

### What to do

- A custom client implementing the protocol: add the three methods, with
  `AsyncMinIOClient`'s signatures (without `stream_object`'s `chunk_size`).
  Without them, the type checker rejects the client.
- Code calling `storage.client.presigned_put_url(storage.key(...))`,
  `stat_object` or `stream_object` directly can switch to `presign_put`,
  `stat` and `read(max_bytes=...)`, which pin the subject prefix.

## 0.320.0 — production guard for e-mail and links

With `ENV=production` and e-mail on (a missing `EMAIL_ENABLED` counts as on),
two new rules fail the boot:

- `EmailSettings`: a dev `SMTP_HOST` (`mailpit`, `mailhog`, port `1025` on
  loopback, the declared default without `SMTP_USERNAME`) and an
  `SMTP_FROM_ADDR` left at the default (`noreply@example.com`), empty,
  without `@`, or on a reserved domain.
- `AuthSettings`: the four `AUTH_*_URL_TEMPLATE` (activation, reset, e-mail
  change and verification) with a local/reserved host or a scheme other than
  `https`. The `http://localhost:3000/...` defaults hit this rule.

### What to do

- Configure a real SMTP and an `SMTP_FROM_ADDR` on your own domain (Gmail
  with an app password on `smtp.gmail.com:587` passes).
- Configure the four templates with `https://` and the app's domain.
- Or, if e-mail is not ready yet, set `EMAIL_ENABLED=false`: the boot passes
  and the routes that send e-mail answer `503 INTEGRATION_DISABLED`.

# Migration 0.31x

Use when upgrading from a version older than these releases: 0.319.0, 0.318.0, 0.316.0, 0.314.0, 0.313.0, 0.312.0 and 0.311.0.

Part of the [Migration guide](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/migration.md).

## 0.319.0 — counts from `bulk_create_values` and `bulk_upsert`

`bulk_create_values` and `bulk_upsert` (`"update"` mode) return `0` when the
database reports `0`; up to 0.318.x a zero `rowcount` became `len(rows)`.
`bulk_upsert(update_columns=[])` raises `ValueError` pointing to
`on_conflict="nothing"`.

### What to do

- Code that treated the result as "always the batch size" now gets the real
  number.
- To insert while skipping what already exists, use
  `bulk_upsert(..., on_conflict="nothing")` (or `returning_ids=True` to learn
  which rows were created).

## 0.318.0 — log readers, empty `log_dir`, header IP and the `/admin` login

Four behavior changes, no signature changes.

1. **Log readers read the backups.** `GET /logs`, `/admin/logs` and
   `read_log_entries` now also read rotated files (`info.log.1`,
   `info.log.2026-10-20`), and `total` counts the backups. `DELETE /logs`
   still only truncates the live file; to delete the backups, use
   `DELETE /logs?delete_backups=true` (or
   `clear_log_files(..., delete_backups=True)`).
2. **An empty `log_dir` is an error.** `make_logs_router(log_dir="")`,
   `clear_log_files("")` and `resolve_log_files("")` raise `ValueError`;
   before, `Path("")` resolved to the working directory.
   `read_log_entries("")` returns nothing. When file logging is off, do not
   mount the logs router with `settings.LOG_DIR`.
3. **The trusted IP header must hold an IP.** `get_client_ip` and
   `get_client_ip_from_scope` validate the value with `ipaddress`; anything
   else falls back to the connection's address. This affects rate limits,
   login throttles and auditing. The edge proxy must **overwrite** the
   header, not append to it.
4. **`/admin/login` has an attempt budget.** 5 failures per identifier every
   900 s by default, in memory; the per-IP budget (20 / 900 s) only turns on
   with `trusted_ip_header`. With more than one process, pass
   `login_throttle=` / `login_ip_throttle=` over Redis; `False` turns it off.

### What to do

- Dashboards or scripts counting `/logs` lines should expect larger numbers.
- Mount the logs router conditionally when `LOG_DIR` can be empty.
- Check that the proxy writes the real IP into the configured header.

## 0.316.0 — `set-password` asks for the factor on an MFA account

`tempest user set-password` on an account with MFA active (and
`AUTH_MFA_ENABLED=True`) now asks for the code — TOTP or recovery code — and
changes the password through `UserAuthService.change_password_with_mfa`.
Without a valid code in three attempts the command exits with code 1 and the
password is left unchanged. Up to 0.315.x the command changed the password
without asking for the factor.

### What to do

1. A script or CI job that runs `set-password` without a terminal on an MFA
   account stops working: nobody is there to type the code.
2. To recover someone who lost the phone **and** the recovery codes, run
   `tempest user mfa-reset --email <e>` (`--yes` outside a terminal) and then
   `set-password`. See [the MFA recipe](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/mfa.md#mfa-reset).
3. To accept a recovery code the command needs the recovery-code table
   (`--recovery-code-model`, default `src.db.models:UserRecoveryCodeModel`).

## 0.316.0 — the second item of `UserAuthService.signup` can be `ActivationWithheld`

The tuple `signup` returns now has three shapes for its second item: `None`
(the account was born active), `ActivationToken` (the link was issued) and
the new `ActivationWithheld(user_id)` (the link was withheld). The third only
comes out with `AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE=false` **and**
`UserAuthService(refuses_email_link=...)` refusing the new account; without
the predicate, runtime behaviour is unchanged. The SDK router already handles
the new type.

### What to do

1. If you call `signup` directly and read `.url` or `.token` from the second
   item, check `isinstance(activation, ActivationToken)` first: with
   `ActivationWithheld` the account exists, inactive and without a link. mypy
   reports `union-attr` where that check is missing.
2. Only `None` authorises issuing the JWT pair right after signup.
3. If you override `signup` and forward to `super()`, adjust the return
   annotation.

## 0.314.0 — Python 3.12 is the new minimum

The SDK drops Python 3.11. `requires-python` moves to `>=3.12`, and the
supported versions become **3.12, 3.13 and 3.14**.

If you are on 3.11 you **stay on 0.313.x**: the installer skips releases whose
`requires-python` excludes the interpreter. Asking for the new version in a
3.11 environment fails before anything is installed. Measured with `uv`:

```text
error: The requested interpreter resolved to Python 3.11.12, which is incompatible with the project's Python requirement: `>=3.12` (from `project.requires-python`)
```

### What to do

1. Move the service interpreter to 3.12 or newer (`uv python pin 3.13`, the
   `Dockerfile` base image, the CI runtime).
2. Set the `requires-python` of your `pyproject.toml` to `>=3.12`.
   `tempest new` already generates it that way, with `target-version = "py312"`
   for ruff and `python_version = "3.12"` for mypy.
3. Run `uv lock` and `uv sync`. With the new floor the lock stops carrying the
   3.11 split: the SDK's own lock dropped `tomli`, `async-timeout` and
   `audioread`, and `numpy`, `scipy` and `librosa` went down to one version
   each.

To stay on 3.11 for now, pin the range:
`uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk>=0.313.0,<0.314.0"`.

## 0.314.0 — social login of an account with TOTP asks for the second factor

`GET /auth/oauth/{provider}/callback` and `POST /auth/oauth/{provider}/token`
now mirror `/auth/login`. When the resolved account has TOTP enrolled (and
`AUTH_MFA_ENABLED=True`), the response carries **no pair and no session
cookie**: it carries `mfa_required=true` + `mfa_token`, and the pair only comes
out of `/auth/mfa/verify`, with `amr == ["ext", "otp"]`. Through 0.313.x the
provider was enough, and the account skipped the factor it had enrolled.

### What to do

1. In the social-login client, handle the challenge as in the password login:
   when `mfa_required` is `true`, ask for the code and call
   `POST /auth/mfa/verify` with the `mfa_token`. An account without MFA does
   not change — the pair stays in the same response, with `amr == ["ext"]`.
2. If you override `UserAuthService.login_with_oauth`, move the logic to the
   new `authenticate_oauth` (resolves the account, issues nothing). The routes
   no longer call `login_with_oauth`, and the router logs a warning when it is
   built and finds the override. Calling `login_with_oauth` directly still
   issues the pair without asking about MFA.
3. If you override `issue_mfa_token`, accept the new
   `amr: Sequence[str] | None = PASSWORD_AMR` and pass it on to `super()`.
   Without it the token carries no first step, and `/auth/mfa/verify` falls
   back to the earlier `["pwd", "otp"]` — the router logs a warning too.

## 0.314.0 — activation and reset links stamp `amr=["email"]`

The pair `POST /auth/activate/{token}` and `POST /auth/password-reset/confirm`
issue to an account **without** MFA now carries `amr == ["email"]`
(`AMR_EMAIL_LINK`) instead of `["pwd"]`: neither checks a password. With TOTP
enrolled, `/auth/mfa/verify` on that challenge issues `["email", "otp"]`.
`refresh` repeats the origin's `amr`, so the session stays `["email"]` after a
rotation.

### What to do

- Code that reads `"pwd" in amr` as "this session started at a login" now sees
  `"email"` on these two paths. If your rule is "any single-factor session",
  compare against `AMR_EMAIL_LINK` as well; if it is "the password was
  checked", the change is the fix you wanted.
- `make_mfa_required_dependency` does not change: `email` is not in
  `MFA_AMR_METHODS`, and the gate refuses the pair as it refused `["pwd"]`.
- An `issue_token_pair` override without `amr=` is still called without the
  keyword, and the pair carries the override's default (`["pwd"]` when it
  delegates to `super()`), as before.

## 0.313.0 — a class ending in `Enum` no longer doubles the type suffix

`enum_type_name` drops one trailing `Enum` from the class name before
appending `_enum`. Only enums with that suffix change:

| Class | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CandidateSlugEnum` | `candidate_slug_enum_enum` | `candidate_slug_enum` |
| `OrderStatus` | `order_status_enum` | `order_status_enum` (same) |

The database keeps the old name until a migration renames the type, and on
PostgreSQL the model now writes the new name in every `INSERT`, `UPDATE` and
`WHERE` on the column. Measured on PostgreSQL 16 with asyncpg, before the
migration: `type "candidate_slug_enum" does not exist` on all three.

### What to do

1. Upgrade the SDK and run `tempest db revision --autogenerate -m "rename enum types"`.
   `sync_enum_types` detects the renamed type (on PostgreSQL through
   `information_schema`, on SQLite through the `CHECK` name) and writes one
   `op.rename_enum_type` per type, with the reverse in `downgrade`:

    ```python
    from alembic import op

    from tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.enum_migrations import EnumColumnRef


    def upgrade() -> None:
        """Rename the enum type to the name without the doubled suffix."""
        op.rename_enum_type(
            "candidate_slug_enum_enum",
            "candidate_slug_enum",
            columns=[EnumColumnRef(table="candidates", column="slug")],
        )
    ```

2. Apply the migration **before** the new code serves traffic (the deploy's
   `alembic upgrade head` already does). `tempest db check` fails while the
   migration is missing, so CI catches the omission.

To keep the old name on a column, pass it explicitly:
`mapped_column(TempestEnum(CandidateSlugEnum, name="candidate_slug_enum_enum"))`.

## 0.313.0 — auth 429s carry their own code

The three throttles of `make_auth_router` stop answering the generic
`TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` code, the same as any other 429 in the app:

| Refusal | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| login over the budget, per e-mail **or** per client | `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` | `LOGIN_THROTTLED` (`LoginThrottledException`) |
| signup over the budget | `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` | `SIGNUP_THROTTLED` (`SignupThrottledException`) |
| wrong MFA code over the budget | `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` | `MFA_THROTTLED` (`MfaThrottledException`) |

The status stays `429`, with `Retry-After` and `details.retry_after_seconds`.
All three subclass `TooManyRequestsException`, so `except
TooManyRequestsException` still catches them. What changes is for whoever
compares the `code`: replace `code == "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS"` with the flow's
code. With `default_message_catalog()`, the `detail` becomes a specific
message (`Too many login attempts — wait a moment and try again`) instead of
`Too many requests`.

## 0.313.0 — the refresh token stores the `amr`, and `/mfa/confirm` answers `200`

The access token now carries the `amr` claim (how the session was
authenticated), and `BaseUserRefreshTokenModel` gained the `amr` column (text,
nullable) so `refresh` can repeat it. Because the column is mapped on the base
model, **migrate the database before upgrading the package** if you use
`refresh_token_model`: without it every pair issuance fails — measured with
SQLite, `POST /auth/signup` with auto-activation answered `500`
(`OperationalError`). Without `refresh_token_model` nothing changes in the
database.

### What to do

1. Generate the migration (`uv run tempest db revision -m "refresh token amr"`,
   or `alembic revision --autogenerate`) or write it by hand, with your table
   name:

    ```python
    import sqlalchemy as sa
    from alembic import op

    revision: str = "0313_refresh_token_amr"
    down_revision: str | None = "<the previous revision>"


    def upgrade() -> None:
        """Add the refresh-token family amr."""
        op.add_column(
            "user_refresh_tokens",
            sa.Column("amr", sa.String(length=64), nullable=True),
        )


    def downgrade() -> None:
        """Drop the refresh-token family amr."""
        op.drop_column("user_refresh_tokens", "amr")
    ```

2. Run `uv run tempest db upgrade` (or `alembic upgrade head`) and only then
   deploy the new version.

Old rows keep `NULL`: their `refresh` issues an access token **without** `amr`,
which `make_mfa_required_dependency` treats as "no second factor".

Two behavior changes come with it:

- **`POST /auth/mfa/confirm` answers `200` with a `LoginResponseSchema`**, no
  longer `204`. Confirming revokes every refresh token of the user, and the new
  pair in the body (or in the cookies, in cookie mode) is what keeps the device
  signed in. A client that checks `status === 204` now checks `200` and stores
  the new pair.
- **`mfa_confirm` revokes the sessions by default.** A caller of the service
  that must keep them passes `revoke_sessions=False`.

### Password reset and link reactivation now ask for the second factor

`POST /auth/password-reset/confirm` and `POST /auth/activate/{token}` now
mirror `/auth/login`: when the account has TOTP enrolled, they do not return
the pair — they return `mfa_required=true` + `mfa_token`, and the pair only
comes out of `/auth/mfa/verify`, with the MFA `amr`. The password is replaced
either way.

A client that called the `confirm` (or the `activate` of a reactivated
account) and stored `access_token` directly must handle the challenge: if
`mfa_required` is `true`, prompt for the code and call `/auth/mfa/verify`. An
account without MFA is unchanged — it still receives the pair in the response
itself. Activating a freshly signed-up account is unchanged too: it never has
a factor.

`ActivationResponseSchema` gained `mfa_required` / `mfa_token`, and
`access_token` / `refresh_token` became optional (`str | None`), as in
`LoginResponseSchema`. Reading the pair from a fresh-account activation is
unchanged.

Password reset now **revokes sessions already open**, in the same transaction
that writes the hash, the way `/auth/mfa/confirm` and `tempest user
set-password` already did: a DB-backed refresh token issued before the reset
can no longer be exchanged for a fresh pair (it answers 401). Access tokens
already issued still live until their TTL. A caller of
`UserAuthService.confirm_password_reset` that needs to keep the sessions passes
`revoke_sessions=False` — an old override signature is still called by the
router, and delegates to the default that revokes. A stateless refresh token
(no `refresh_token_model`) has no row to revoke and stays valid until it
expires.

## 0.312.0 — Mercado Pago: expired Pix and chargeback search

Two behaviour changes, both measured in the sandbox on 2026-10-10.

**An expired Pix is now `EXPIRED`.** An order Mercado Pago returns as
`canceled` / `expired` is now `PaymentStatus.EXPIRED`, and the webhook
delivers it as `PixEventType.CHARGE_EXPIRED`. Up to 0.311.0 it came out as
`CANCELLED` / `CHARGE_CANCELLED`. If your service handled expiry in the
cancellation branch, handle both:

```python
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.payment import PaymentStatusEnum, PixCharge


def is_closed_unpaid(charge: PixCharge) -> bool:
    """Tell whether a Pix charge ended without being paid."""
    return charge.status in {PaymentStatusEnum.CANCELLED, PaymentStatusEnum.EXPIRED}
```

**`search_chargebacks` requires `payment_id`.** The search answered `400`
without that filter, including in the only shape the method accepted
(`limit` / `offset`), so it never worked. Now:

| Before | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `await client.search_chargebacks(limit=10)` → always `400` | `await client.search_chargebacks(payment_id="123")` → `ChargebackSearchResponse` |
| `dict[str, Any]` | `found.paging.total`, `found.results` (items still `dict[str, Any]`) |

## 0.311.0 — Mercado Pago: the Payments API left the SDK

Mercado Pago's dashboard labels the Payments API (`/v1/payments`) *"Esta API
será descontinuada em breve"* (this API will be discontinued soon), and the
SDK now charges through the Orders API. If you used the Payments path,
switch like this:

| Before | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `client.create_payment(body=PaymentRequest(...))` with Pix | `MercadoPagoPixProvider(http).create_pix_charge(PixChargeRequest(...))` |
| `client.create_payment(...)` with a card `token` | `MercadoPagoCardProvider(http).create_card_charge(CardChargeRequest(...))` |
| `create_pix_payment` / `get_pix_payment` / `parse_pix_payment` | `create_pix_charge` / `get_pix_charge` — the QR is on `PixCharge.br_code` and `qr_code_base64` |
| `client.get_payment(id)` | `get_pix_charge(order_id)` / `get_card_charge(order_id)`, or `client.get_order(order_id)` |
| `client.update_payment(id, body={"capture": True})` | `capture_card_charge(order_id)` |
| `client.update_payment(id, body={"status": "cancelled"})` | `cancel_pix_charge(order_id)` / `cancel_card_charge(order_id)` |
| `client.create_refund(id, ...)` | `refund_card_charge(order_id, amount_cents=...)` |
| `PixPayment`, `Payment` | `PixCharge`, `CardCharge`, or the generated `Order` |
| the 7 V1/V2 in-store QR and old dynamic QR operations | no replacement in this SDK: the spec itself marks them `deprecated`, and the spec's Orders API only declares `type: online` |

**Removed with no direct replacement** (the equivalent, where one exists, is
the generated `Order` or the `PixCharge` / `CardCharge` contracts):

- **`MercadoPagoClient` methods:** `create_payment`, `search_payments`,
  `get_payment`, `update_payment`, `cancel_payment`, `create_refund`,
  `list_refunds`, `get_refund`, and the 7 in-store QR ones —
  `create_instore_order_v1`, `delete_instore_order_v1`,
  `create_instore_order_v2`, `get_instore_order_v2`,
  `delete_instore_order_v2`, `create_dynamic_qr_order`,
  `create_qr_tramma_dynamic`.
- **Functions and constants:** `create_pix_payment`, `get_pix_payment`,
  `parse_pix_payment`, `PAYMENTS_PATH`.
- **Models and enums:** `PixPayment`, `PixPointOfInteraction`,
  `PixTransactionData`, `Payment`, `PaymentRequest`, `PaymentPayer`,
  `PaymentPayer2`, `PaymentCard`, `PaymentCardCardholder`, `PaymentItem`,
  `PaymentAdditionalInfo`, `PaymentAdditionalInfoPayer`,
  `PaymentAdditionalInfoShipments`, `PaymentTransactionDetails`,
  `PaymentOperationType`, `PaymentPaymentTypeId`, `PaymentProcessingMode`,
  `PaymentSearchResult`, `SearchPaymentsRange`, `PaymentUpdateRequest`,
  `PaymentUpdateRequestStatus`, `CancelPaymentBody`, `RefundRequest`,
  `CreateRefundResponse`, `CreateRefundResponseSource`, `GetRefundResponse`,
  `GetRefundResponseSource`, `ListRefundsResponse`,
  `ListRefundsResponseSource`, and `mercado_pago`'s `PaymentStatus`. The
  **canonical** `PaymentStatus`, from `integrations.payment`, stays — it is
  what the contracts use.

**Types that changed:**

- `Order.status`, `Order.status_detail`, `OrderTransactionPayment.status` and
  `OrderTransactionPayment.status_detail` go from an enum to `Enum | str`:
  the sandbox returned values outside the list. An exhaustive `match` over
  the enum needs a branch for the string.
- `get_authenticated_user()` returns `AuthenticatedUser` instead of
  `dict[str, Any]`: replace `user["id"]` with `user.id` (what is not declared
  is in `user.model_extra`).
- Two enums got names of their own:
  `ListPaymentMethodsResponseItemProcessingModesItem` (the
  `list_payment_methods` processing mode) and
  `UpdateAdvancedPaymentBodyStatus` (the `update_advanced_payment` body
  status).

Three differences that need more than a rename:

1. **The id changes shape.** An order id is text (`ORD…`), not a number. If
   you stored the payment id as an integer, the column becomes text.
2. **The webhook points at another resource.** The notification should now
   name the order — that is what the provider's document describes
   (`order.created` / `order.updated` actions); the live delivery observed on
   2026-11-13 carried `type=order`, and `event.event` is `ORDER` since
   v0.358.0. Replace manual reads of `data.id` with
   `make_mercado_pago_webhook_delivery_dependency`, and tick the Order event
   in the application's webhook settings.
3. **The credential must come from an "Orders API" application.** Measured:
   a test seller's Checkout Pro application answers `401 Unauthorized use of
   live credentials` to a direct charge. The
   [test accounts and credentials](https://mauriciobenjamin700.github.io/tempest-fastapi-sdk/en/recipes/mercado-pago-sandbox.md) recipe
   shows the way.
